Accountable obligation owner.value: Controller owns the ERISA plan control matrix and the named-fiduciary register; any change to a named fiduciary or a delegation instrument escalates to the General Counsel and the plan Benefits Committee

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — ERISA §402(a)(1)-(2) and §405(c)(1) (29 U.S.C. §§1102, 1105), 29 CFR 2550.404a-1 and 29 CFR 2560.503-1(b) re-read on eCFR at each quarterly matrix refresh; EBSA sub-regulatory position taken from ERISA Interpretive Bulletin 75-8 (FR-13 through FR-17) on who is a fiduciary

In-scope processes.value: Every ERISA-covered plan this insurer sponsors, insures or administers as recordkeeper/TPA — Retirement/401(k), Group Life, Group Disability, Group Health, Group Long-Term Care, Group Annuities and Pension Risk Transfer contracts — from plan-document intake, through named-fiduciary appointment and delegation, to the plan financial statements that feed Form 5500 Schedule H

In-scope systems.value: Plan trust, contribution, distribution and plan-expense ledgers that roll into Schedule H Parts I and II; the named-fiduciary register and executed delegation instruments sit in the document management repository keyed by plan number + EIN

Compliance procedure documented.value: ERISA Named Fiduciary & Delegation Procedure (who may be appointed, how §405(c)(1) delegation is executed under the plan instrument, how acceptance is captured) plus the ERISA Plan ICFR Control Matrix — one row per plan per financial-statement assertion: contributions, distributions/benefit payments, participant loans, investment income, plan expenses

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Financial Officer and ratified by the plan Benefits Committee in minutes; re-approved annually and on any plan amendment, trustee change or fiduciary appointment change

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Control operates continuously; the matrix rolls up to the Form 5500 due date — last day of the 7th month after plan year end (July 31 for a calendar-year plan), extended to October 15 by Form 5558 — and to the 120-day post-plan-year-end audit readiness date

Deadline reminders configured.value: Control-owner attestations fall due 20 business days after each quarter end; automated reminders fire at plan year end +30 (trial balance), +60 (draft plan financials) and +120 days (auditor fieldwork start) for every plan on the register

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Plan instruments, named-fiduciary acceptance letters, delegation resolutions, trustee agreements and every dated version of the control matrix retained six years from the Form 5500 filing date per ERISA §107, and for as long as any participant benefit may become due per ERISA §209

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: A plan running with no named fiduciary identified in the plan instrument, or a delegation made outside the instrument's stated procedure, is raised as a fiduciary control breach with root cause, corrective plan instrument amendment and the Benefits Committee ratification date recorded as the disposition

Remediation sign-off captured.value: General Counsel signs every fiduciary appointment correction and every retroactive delegation ratification before the control matrix row is returned to effective

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All ERISA plans on the plan register at quarter end (sponsored plus administered), each plan's named-fiduciary appointment record, and every delegation instrument executed or amended during the period

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on the §402(a) requirement — a plan with no named fiduciary in the instrument, or a delegation lacking the instrument's documented procedure, is an outright fail; any single fail is reported to the Benefits Committee and the Audit Committee at their next sitting

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation operates continuously; the matrix is tested quarterly over new and amended plans and 100% annually before the independent qualified public accountant starts plan-audit fieldwork

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Tester must not maintain the plan register, own any control-matrix row, or have drafted any sampled delegation instrument

Evidence location for test results.value: ERISA fiduciary control workpaper (plan register extract, dated matrix version, plan instruments, delegation instruments, exception log) in the compliance evidence repository filed under Plan Year / Plan Number / EIN

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Plan register with named-fiduciary schedule keyed to plan number and EIN, the governing plan instruments and delegation resolutions, producible to an EBSA regional-office investigator on an ERISA §504 document request within the 30-day response window stated in the request letter

Regulator response path.value: Corporate Secretary logs the EBSA inquiry on receipt; General Counsel owns the response to EBSA regional-office document requests and clears every statement about who held fiduciary status before it leaves the building

checklist.step: Refresh the register of ERISA plans the insurer sponsors or administers
actions: In Workday open Benefits ▸ Plan Setup and export every benefit plan with its plan number (001, 501, 502…), EIN, plan type code and plan year end.
Ask Group Operations for the list of client plans where the insurer acts as recordkeeper or TPA, with contract number and plan sponsor EIN, and append those rows.
Mark each row ERISA-covered or excluded, and for excluded rows name the exclusion (governmental plan, church plan, payroll practice, voluntary employee-pay-all arrangement under 29 CFR 2510.3-1(j)).
Send the draft register to the Benefits Analyst for confirmation that no plan added or terminated in the quarter is missing.
Save the confirmed register as ERISA-plan-register-<yyyy-qq>.xlsx in the document management repository.
checklist.done: the register lists every plan with plan number, EIN, plan year end and an ERISA-covered / excluded call with a named exclusion basis.

checklist.step: Pull the governing plan instrument and trust agreement for every register row
actions: For each plan number open the plan folder and retrieve the executed base plan document, every amendment in effect at quarter end, the adoption agreement and the trust agreement or group annuity contract funding it.
Check each document is signed and dated — an unsigned restatement does not count as the plan instrument.
Where an amendment is missing, request the execution copy from the plan sponsor's Corporate Secretary and record the request date on the register row.
Build a document index per plan showing base document date, amendment numbers and effective dates, and attach it to the register row.
checklist.done: every register row links to a signed, dated plan instrument set with a complete amendment index.

checklist.step: Read the §402(a) named-fiduciary clause in each plan instrument
actions: Open each plan document and locate the article headed 'Named Fiduciary', 'Plan Administrator' or 'Allocation of Responsibilities'.

Confirm the clause either names a person/committee outright or states a procedure by which the named fiduciary is identified, as ERISA §402(a)(2) requires — a document that merely says 'the Company' with no appointing procedure fails.
Copy the exact clause text and its section number onto the register row alongside the identified named fiduciary.
Flag any plan whose clause is silent, circular or names a dissolved committee for plan amendment, and open a legal matter for it.
checklist.done: each plan row carries the quoted named-fiduciary clause, its section number and the identified fiduciary, or a raised amendment matter.

checklist.step: Confirm the trustee and funding vehicle behind each plan's assets
actions: For each funded plan read the trust agreement to identify the trustee, whether it is directed or discretionary, and the custodian holding plan assets.

For insured welfare plans and group annuity contracts, record the contract number and confirm whether the ERISA §401(b)(2) guaranteed-benefit-policy exclusion applies so trust assets are correctly scoped.
Reconcile the trustee named in the trust agreement to the trustee named in the plan instrument and resolve any mismatch with Regulatory Counsel before quarter close.
Record trustee, custodian and funding vehicle on the register row.
checklist.done: trustee, custodian and funding vehicle are recorded per plan and agree between the plan instrument and the trust agreement.

checklist.step: Capture a signed acceptance from every named fiduciary and committee member
actions: Issue an acceptance-of-appointment letter to each named fiduciary and each Benefits Committee member stating the plans covered, the responsibilities accepted and the ERISA §404(a)(1) prudence standard.
Send via DocuSign with the plan number list in the envelope name; chase any envelope open more than 10 business days.
File the executed acceptance in the plan folder and write the signature date onto the named-fiduciary register.
Remove any individual who has left the role, and issue the successor's acceptance before the seat is recorded as filled.
checklist.done: every named fiduciary and committee seat has a current, dated signed acceptance on file with no vacant seats.

checklist.step: Map the delegation procedure each plan instrument actually permits
actions: Locate the ERISA §405(c)(1) allocation/delegation clause in each plan document and copy the exact mechanism it requires — committee resolution, written designation by the named fiduciary, or board action.
Record which responsibilities the instrument permits to be delegated (investment management, claims adjudication, recordkeeping) and which it reserves.
Write a one-page delegation rule sheet per plan and circulate it to the Benefits Administrator and the Controller so delegations are not executed by email.
Flag any plan that has no delegation procedure at all — under §405(c)(1) no protected delegation is possible there until the instrument is amended.
checklist.done: each plan has a delegation rule sheet quoting the instrument's mechanism and listing delegable versus reserved responsibilities.

checklist.step: Record every live delegation against the instrument's mechanism
actions: Open a delegation register entry for each live delegation: plan number, responsibility delegated, delegate name, instrument clause relied on, executing document, execution date and expiry or review date.
Attach the executing document — committee resolution extract, written designation, or investment management agreement naming the delegate as an ERISA §3(38) investment manager.
Reject any delegation whose executing document does not match the mechanism on the plan's delegation rule sheet and send it back to the Benefits Committee for proper execution.
Set an annual review task on every open delegation entry.
checklist.done: every live delegation has a register entry, an attached executing document matching the instrument's mechanism and a review date.

checklist.step: Prove the delegated service providers meet the §408(b)(2) disclosure condition
actions: For each delegate that is a covered service provider, pull the 29 CFR 2550.408b-2(c)(1) disclosure showing services, fiduciary/registered-investment-adviser status, direct compensation, indirect compensation and its payer.
Check the disclosure was furnished reasonably in advance of the contract date and that any change was disclosed within 60 days of the provider knowing of it.

Where a disclosure is missing, issue the written request the regulation requires and, if unanswered within 90 days, report the provider to EBSA and start termination review with the Benefits Committee.
Link the disclosure and the executed services agreement to the delegation register entry.
checklist.done: every delegate has a current 408(b)(2) disclosure linked to its delegation entry, or a documented written request and escalation.

checklist.step: Build the ERISA plan control matrix rows for each plan and assertion
actions: Create one matrix row per plan per assertion: participant contributions and remittance timeliness, benefit distributions, participant loans, investment income and valuation, plan expenses and fee allocation, participant data completeness.
For each row record the control objective, control owner, frequency, whether it is preventive or detective, the system of record and the evidence artifact produced.
Tie each row back to the fiduciary duty it supports — §404(a)(1)(A) exclusive purpose, §404(a)(1)(B) prudence, §404(a)(1)(D) documents-and-instruments — and to the plan instrument clause.
Have each named control owner confirm ownership in AuditBoard before the matrix version is baselined.
checklist.done: the matrix has a complete, owner-confirmed row for every plan and assertion with the fiduciary duty referenced.

checklist.step: Wire the matrix to the ledger accounts that feed Schedule H
actions: For each plan, list the trust and plan-expense GL accounts that populate Schedule H Part I (assets and liabilities) and Part II (income and expenses).
Map each account to the control-matrix row that governs it so no Schedule H line is left uncontrolled.
Run the plan trial balance for the period and agree total net assets to the trustee/custodian statement to the dollar; investigate any difference over $1,000 before sign-off.
Record the mapping and the reconciliation reference on each matrix row.
checklist.done: every Schedule H line traces to at least one matrix row and the plan trial balance agrees to the custodian statement.

checklist.step: Review the recordkeeper's SOC 1 report and complete the user-entity controls
actions: Obtain the current SOC 1 Type II report for each recordkeeper, custodian and claims administrator, covering a period that includes the plan year end.
Read Section IV for exceptions and Section V for complementary user-entity controls, and list every user-entity control the insurer must itself perform.
Add a control-matrix row for each user-entity control with an owner, and note any SOC 1 exception plus the service organisation's remediation statement.
Where the report period leaves a gap to plan year end, obtain a bridge letter from the service organisation covering the gap.
checklist.done: each service organisation has a current SOC 1 plus bridge letter, and every complementary user-entity control is an owned matrix row.

checklist.step: Run the quarterly control-owner attestation over the matrix
actions: Launch the quarterly attestation campaign in AuditBoard to every control owner 5 business days after quarter end, due within 20 business days.
Require each owner to answer: did the control operate every period, is the evidence attached, were there failures, and did any plan amendment change the control.
Chase non-responders at day 10 and day 15 and escalate anyone outstanding at day 20 to their department head.
Baseline the attested matrix as the quarter's version of record and lock it against edits.
checklist.done: 100% of control owners have attested with evidence attached and the quarter's matrix version is baselined and locked.

checklist.step: Take the appointments and delegations to the Benefits Committee for ratification
actions: Prepare the committee pack: named-fiduciary register, new and amended delegations, 408(b)(2) disclosure status and any open fiduciary control breach.
Record in the minutes each appointment, each delegation and the instrument clause relied on — minutes are the evidence that the delegation followed the plan's procedure.
Capture the committee's monitoring decision for each delegate (retain, place under review, terminate) with the reason.
Post the approved minutes to the board portal and link them to the delegation register entries.
checklist.done: minutes record every appointment and delegation with its instrument clause, and each is linked to the delegation register.

checklist.step: Log and dispose of fiduciary control breaks
actions: Raise an issue for each break: plan with no named fiduciary, delegation executed outside the instrument's mechanism, vacant committee seat, missing 408(b)(2) disclosure, failed matrix control.
Assign a root cause (plan amendment not executed, committee turnover, provider onboarded without disclosure) and an accountable owner.
Set a remediation date, and for any break touching plan assets ask Regulatory Counsel whether a prohibited transaction or VFCP correction filing is needed.
Track each issue to closure with the corrective document attached, and carry open issues into the next quarter's attestation as mandatory items.
checklist.done: every break has an issue with root cause, owner, remediation date and a decision on whether a correction filing is required.

checklist.step: File the fiduciary and control evidence for the ERISA §107 retention period
actions: Move the quarter's plan register, plan instruments, acceptance letters, delegation register export, SOC 1 reports and baselined matrix into the evidence repository under Plan Year / Plan Number / EIN.
Apply the six-years-from-Form-5500-filing retention label required by ERISA §107, and the longer benefit-determination label required by ERISA §209 to participant-level records.
Confirm the repository index makes the record retrievable by plan number, EIN and named fiduciary name.
Run a legal-hold check so no record under an open EBSA inquiry or participant claim is purged on schedule.
checklist.done: the quarter's evidence is filed, labelled for §107 and §209 retention, retrievable by plan number and screened for legal hold.

testing.step: Build the population of ERISA plans and delegations for the period
actions: Extract every benefit plan from Workday Benefits ▸ Plan Setup with plan number, EIN and plan year end, independently of the register the Benefits Administrator produced.
Add administered client plans from the Group Operations contract listing so recordkeeping engagements cannot be omitted.
Extract every delegation register entry created or amended in the period from the GRC platform.
Sign the population as complete, recording extraction date, filters and row counts in the workpaper.
testing.done: the plan and delegation population is independently extracted, row-counted and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the audit population to the Form 5500 filing history and the plan register
actions: Compare the population to the prior year's filed Form 5500 series by plan number and EIN using the EFAST2 filing search.
Compare the population to the Controller's ERISA plan register and list every plan in one source but not the other.
Obtain a written explanation for each difference (plan merged, terminated, newly adopted, excluded as a payroll practice) and verify it against the plan document or termination resolution.
Resolve all differences before drawing the sample — an unreconciled population invalidates the test.
testing.done: population, register and prior-year 5500 filings reconcile, with each difference explained and documented.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of plans newly adopted, amended, merged or terminated in the period, and 100% of plans with more than 100 participants with account balances.
Add 15 remaining plans selected by seeded random draw, for a minimum of 25 plans in total.
Take 100% of delegations executed in the period plus 10 legacy delegations by seeded random draw.
Record the seed, population size, selection date and selection logic so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
testing.done: a reproducible sample is drawn covering all new/amended and large plans plus all period delegations.

testing.step: Re-perform the named-fiduciary determination from the plan document
actions: Open the signed plan instrument and amendments for each sampled plan without first reading the register entry.
Locate the §402(a) clause and form your own conclusion on who the named fiduciary is or how the instrument says one is identified.
Compare to the register entry; a different name, a clause that names no one and states no appointing procedure, or a reliance on an unsigned restatement is an exception.
Capture the clause text and the document signature page into the workpaper as support.
testing.done: each sampled plan has an independent named-fiduciary conclusion with the clause and signature page captured.

testing.step: Test each sampled delegation against the instrument's stated mechanism
actions: Read the plan's §405(c)(1) clause and note the exact mechanism it requires before opening the executing document.

Open the executing document and confirm the right body acted, the responsibility delegated is one the instrument permits to be delegated, and the execution date pre-dates the delegate first performing the work.
Trace the delegation to the Benefits Committee minutes that ratified it and confirm the minutes cite the same clause.
Treat an email instruction, a service agreement with no corresponding resolution, or a delegation of a reserved responsibility as a fail.
testing.done: every sampled delegation is supported by a correctly executed instrument, minuted ratification and a pre-dated effective date.

testing.step: Verify fiduciary acceptances and check for vacant seats
actions: Pull the signed acceptance letter for each named fiduciary and committee member on the sampled plans and check the signature date and the plans listed.
Reconcile the committee roster to the HR leaver report for the period and identify any seat vacated without a successor acceptance.
Compute the gap in days between a departure and the successor's acceptance and record any gap over 30 days as an exception.
Confirm every acceptance references the plans it covers — a generic acceptance naming no plan is a documentation fail.
testing.done: every sampled seat has a dated, plan-specific acceptance and every vacancy gap is measured and logged.

testing.step: Trace matrix controls to operating evidence and to Schedule H lines
actions: For 3 matrix rows per sampled plan, request the evidence artifact for a named period and check it is dated, signed by the control owner and covers the stated population.
Trace each tested row to the Schedule H line it supports and confirm no Schedule H asset, income or expense line is left without a mapped control.
Re-perform one plan-level reconciliation of net assets to the custodian statement and agree the closing balance.
Record any control operating without evidence as ineffective regardless of the owner's attestation.
testing.done: sampled matrix rows are evidenced, mapped to Schedule H lines and one net-asset reconciliation is re-performed and agreed.

testing.step: Verify service-provider disclosure and SOC 1 coverage on the sample
actions: For each sampled delegate, confirm a 29 CFR 2550.408b-2(c)(1) disclosure exists and was furnished before the contract date.
Recompute the SOC 1 coverage: report period start and end against the plan year end, and confirm a bridge letter covers any gap.
Check each complementary user-entity control listed in the SOC 1 has a matrix row with an owner and evidence.
Flag any SOC 1 exception with no corresponding matrix row addressing the residual risk.
testing.done: each sampled delegate has a pre-contract 408(b)(2) disclosure and SOC 1 coverage with all user-entity controls owned.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception recording plan number, EIN, what failed, the fiduciary duty implicated and the participant impact if any.
Assign a root cause (instrument never amended, committee turnover, delegation by email, provider onboarded without disclosure) and an accountable owner.
Set a remediation date and, where plan assets or benefit payments were affected, refer to Regulatory Counsel for a decision on EBSA Voluntary Fiduciary Correction Program filing.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and a documented VFCP referral decision where assets were affected.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance named-fiduciary threshold and against the matrix effectiveness rate.
State the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — with the workpaper references behind it.
Have the reviewer, who owns no control-matrix row and drafted no sampled delegation, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and all open fiduciary breaches to the Benefits Committee and the Audit Committee at their next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and committee reporting date is filed in the evidence repository.

checklist.step: Scope the annual ERISA key-control audit from a documented risk assessment
actions: List every ERISA process in scope — contribution remittance, distributions, loans, claims adjudication, investment decisions, participant data, recordkeeper cyber — and score each on inherent risk, participant impact and prior-year deficiency history.
Take the prior-year IQPA management letter and the prior-year deficiency log and force every open item into this year's scope.
Set the fieldwork window so the report issues within 120 days after the end of the plan year, ahead of IQPA fieldwork.
Present the scoping memo to the Audit Committee for approval and record the approval date in AuditBoard.
checklist.done: an Audit-Committee-approved scoping memo exists with risk scores, prior-year carry-forwards and a fieldwork window closing by plan year end +120 days.

checklist.step: Publish the prudence-file standard the tests will measure decisions against
actions: Write the standard: every fiduciary decision file must show the question asked, the alternatives considered, the data relied on and its date, the advisers consulted, the conclusion and the decision-maker with date.

Anchor it to 29 CFR 2550.404a-1(b)(2) — the fiduciary must give appropriate consideration to the facts relevant to the decision — and state plainly that a defensible outcome with no process on file is still a fail.
Circulate to the Benefits Committee, Investment Operations and Claims leadership so the standard is known before it is tested against.
Have the General Counsel approve the standard and record the approval date.
checklist.done: a counsel-approved prudence-file standard is published to all decision-making functions before fieldwork opens.

checklist.step: Write the test script for contribution remittance timeliness
actions: Define the control: participant deferrals and loan repayments must be segregated from general assets on the earliest date they can reasonably be segregated, and no later than the 15th business day of the month following withholding (29 CFR 2510.3-102), with the 7-business-day safe harbour for plans under 100 participants.
Specify the population source: payroll withholding registers matched to trust deposit dates.
Set the sample at 40 pay periods per plan, or 100% where the plan had a prior-year late remittance.
Set the exception definition: any deposit later than the plan's established earliest-reasonable pattern, and require lost-earnings computation on every one.
checklist.done: a signed test script exists with the regulatory deposit standard, population source, sample size and exception definition.

checklist.step: Write the test scripts for distributions, loans and participant data
actions: For distributions: test spousal consent where required, correct vesting percentage applied, tax withholding elected and the distribution authorised by someone with delegated authority.

For loans: test the loan does not exceed the lesser of $50,000 or 50% of the vested balance, the term is within 5 years unless a principal residence loan, and repayments are amortised level and at least quarterly.
For participant data: test date of birth, date of hire, compensation and hours against the sponsor's payroll file, because a benefit computed on wrong data is a §404(a)(1)(D) failure.
Set sample sizes at 25 items per control with 100% coverage of transactions above $100,000.
checklist.done: test scripts for distributions, loans and participant data are written with named attributes and sample sizes.

checklist.step: Write the test script for claims adjudication against 29 CFR 2560.503-1
actions: Define the timing attributes: group health post-service determinations within 30 days, disability determinations within 45 days with two 30-day extensions, pension claims within 90 days with a 90-day extension, and appeals within 60 days.

Define the content attributes from 29 CFR 2560.503-1(g): the specific reason, the plan provision relied on, a description of any additional material needed and why, and a statement of the claimant's right to bring a §502(a) civil action.
Set the population as every adverse benefit determination and appeal decision in the plan year, sampled 40 per plan type with 100% coverage of appeals that were upheld.
State that a determination missing the §502(a) rights statement is a fail even if the outcome was correct, because 29 CFR 2560.503-1(l) then deems the claimant to have exhausted remedies.
checklist.done: a claims test script exists with per-plan-type timing clocks, the (g) content attributes and the deemed-exhaustion fail rule.

checklist.step: Write the test script for recordkeeper cybersecurity against Compliance Assistance Release 2021-01
actions: Take the twelve EBSA Cybersecurity Program Best Practices as the attribute list: formal programme, annual risk assessment, third-party audit of controls, defined roles, strong access controls, cloud-provider assurance, training, secure SDLC, business resilience, encryption in transit and at rest, incident response, and periodic penetration testing.
Define the evidence for each attribute — the recordkeeper's most recent third-party control audit, its penetration test summary, and its incident-response plan test record.
Add the EBSA Online Security Tips distribution check: participants must have been given the guidance in the annual participant communication.
Set the test as 100% of recordkeepers and custodians holding participant data, not a sample.
checklist.done: a cyber test script covers all twelve EBSA best practices across 100% of recordkeepers with named evidence per attribute.

checklist.step: Extract and reconcile the test populations
actions: Pull for the plan year: payroll withholding registers with deposit dates, all distributions and loans with amounts and authorisers, all adverse benefit determinations with receipt and decision timestamps, and all fiduciary investment decision records.
Reconcile each extract to its system of record control total — contributions to the trust ledger, distributions to the 1099-R file, claims to the claims platform decision counts.
Document extraction date, filters, row counts and reconciliation differences, and clear every difference before sampling.
Hand the frozen populations to the audit team with a signed completeness statement.
checklist.done: each population is extracted, reconciled to a control total, frozen and signed as complete.

checklist.step: Perform contribution remittance testing and compute lost earnings on every late deposit
actions: For each sampled pay period, compare the withholding date to the trust deposit date and to the plan's fastest historical deposit lag — that lag, not the outer limit, is the standard.
For every late deposit, run the EBSA Voluntary Fiduciary Correction Program Online Calculator to compute lost earnings from the earliest reasonable segregation date to the deposit date.
Record the participant count and dollar amount affected and hand the computation to the Controller for funding.
Refer any pattern of lateness to Regulatory Counsel for a VFCP application decision and a prohibited-transaction excise tax assessment on Form 5330.
checklist.done: every sampled remittance has a lag computed, every late one has lost earnings quantified and a correction route decided.

checklist.step: Perform distribution, loan and participant data testing
actions: Open each sampled distribution in the recordkeeping system and check the vesting percentage against the plan's vesting schedule and the participant's service history.
Confirm the authoriser held delegated authority on the transaction date by checking the delegation register, not the current org chart.
For each sampled loan, recompute the maximum available amount and the amortisation schedule and compare to what was issued.
Compare date of birth, date of hire, hours and eligible compensation to the sponsor payroll file and log any field mismatch as a participant-data exception.
checklist.done: each sampled distribution, loan and data record is re-performed against plan terms and payroll source with exceptions logged.

checklist.step: Perform claims adjudication testing on the sampled determinations
actions: For each sampled claim open the claim file and record the date the claim was received, the date the determination letter was issued and any extension notice with its stated reason.
Compute elapsed days against the plan-type clock and flag anything over, including extensions taken without the required written notice before the original period expired.
Read the determination letter against the 29 CFR 2560.503-1(g) content attributes one by one and tick or fail each.

For disability claims, additionally check the (g)(1)(vii) attributes: discussion of disagreement with treating-provider or SSA determinations and disclosure of the internal rule or guideline relied on.
checklist.done: each sampled determination has a computed day count and an attribute-by-attribute content result against 2560.503-1(g).

checklist.step: Test the prudence file behind each sampled fiduciary decision
actions: Select every investment lineup change, recordkeeper selection or fee decision taken in the plan year plus 10 routine monitoring decisions.
Open the decision file and test it against the published prudence-file standard element by element: question, alternatives, data and its date, advisers, conclusion, decision-maker and date.
Confirm the committee minutes record the decision and that the materials the committee actually saw are attached, not reconstructed afterwards.
Fail any file where the conclusion is sound but the process is undocumented — that is the exact failure mode ERISA §404(a)(1)(B) punishes.
checklist.done: each sampled fiduciary decision has a documented element-by-element prudence-file result with committee materials attached.

checklist.step: Grade every deficiency for severity and quantify participant impact
actions: Apply the rubric: material weakness where participants could be systematically underpaid or benefits misstated; significant deficiency where a deemed-exhaustion event or a repeat late-remittance pattern occurred; deficiency otherwise.
Quantify participant impact in dollars and headcount for every finding — an ungraded finding cannot be prioritised.
Check each finding against the prior-year deficiency log and mark repeats, which are graded one level higher automatically.
Have a second auditor peer-review every severity grade before the findings go to management.
checklist.done: every deficiency is graded, quantified, marked for repeat status and peer-reviewed.

checklist.step: Agree remediation plans with owners within 30 days of the report
actions: Issue the draft findings to each process owner and hold a closing meeting within 10 business days of fieldwork close.
Require each owner to submit a remediation plan with named actions, an accountable individual and a completion date within 30 days of the final report.
Reject plans that only add monitoring where the control itself failed — the fix must address the root cause.
Load each plan into AuditBoard with a 90-day re-test date on every high-severity item.
checklist.done: every finding has an owner-signed remediation plan within 30 days and a scheduled 90-day re-test for high-severity items.

checklist.step: Re-test remediated controls within 90 days and close only on evidence
actions: At the 90-day mark pull a fresh sample of transactions processed after the remediation date, never the transactions that were originally tested.
Re-perform the original test attributes and record the new exception rate against the same threshold.
Close the finding only where the re-test passes; a management assertion of completion without transaction evidence keeps the finding open.
Escalate to the Audit Committee any high-severity finding still open at 90 days with the reason and a revised date.
checklist.done: each high-severity finding is re-tested on fresh post-remediation transactions and closed only on passing evidence.

checklist.step: Report to the Audit Committee and file the audit evidence
actions: Issue the report within 120 days after the end of the plan year with scope, conclusion per control, deficiency log by severity and quantified participant impact.
Present to the Audit Committee and the Benefits Committee, and give the IQPA a copy so the plan audit can rely on the work.
File the complete audit file — scoping memo, scripts, populations, samples, workpapers, remediation plans, re-test evidence — in the evidence repository under Plan Year.
Apply the ERISA §107 six-year retention label running from the Form 5500 filing date.
checklist.done: the report is issued within 120 days of plan year end, presented to both committees and the audit file is retained under §107.

testing.step: Rebuild the audit population independently from the systems of record
actions: Re-extract contributions, distributions, loans and adverse benefit determinations for the plan year directly from source, without using the audit team's frozen files.
Compare row counts and control totals to the populations the audit relied on and quantify any difference.
Where the audit population is short, identify what the filter excluded and whether the exclusion was disclosed in the scoping memo.
Record the reconciliation in the quality-review workpaper before any sampling.
testing.done: the audit populations are independently rebuilt and reconciled, with every difference quantified and explained.

testing.step: Reconcile the tested scope to the approved audit plan and the prior-year issues
actions: List every control in the Audit-Committee-approved scoping memo and tick off those with completed workpapers.
Confirm every prior-year deficiency and IQPA management-letter comment was carried into scope and actually tested.
Identify any control descoped after approval and confirm the Audit Committee approved the descope in minutes.
Log unexplained scope reductions as a governance exception, not a housekeeping note.
testing.done: tested scope reconciles to the approved plan, and every descope has minuted Audit Committee approval.

testing.step: Draw and document a re-performance sample from the audit's own workpapers
actions: Take 100% of workpapers supporting high-severity deficiencies and 100% of contribution remittance testing.
Add 20 items by seeded random draw across the distribution, loan, claims and prudence-file scripts.
Record the seed, population size and selection date so the sample is reproducible.
Note for each selected item the original tester so segregation from the reviewer can be proven.
testing.done: a reproducible re-performance sample is drawn covering all high-severity workpapers and the zero-tolerance controls.

testing.step: Re-perform the remittance timeliness judgement and the lost-earnings maths
actions: For 10 sampled pay periods, recompute the lag from withholding date to trust deposit date from the payroll register and the trust statement.
Recompute the plan's earliest-reasonable segregation pattern from the fastest deposits in the year and compare it to the standard the audit applied.
Re-run the EBSA VFCP Online Calculator for each late deposit and agree the lost-earnings figure to the cent.
Confirm the lost earnings were actually funded to the trust and allocated to affected participant accounts.
testing.done: remittance lags, the earliest-reasonable standard and lost-earnings amounts are re-computed, agreed and traced to funding.

testing.step: Re-perform claims-timeliness and content conclusions in the claims system
actions: Open each sampled claim in the claims platform, read the receipt and decision timestamps from the audit trail rather than the summary screen, and recompute elapsed days.
Read the issued determination letter and independently score the 29 CFR 2560.503-1(g) content attributes before looking at the audit's result.
Compare your conclusion to the auditor's and treat any difference — including a right answer supported by the wrong cited provision — as an exception.
Capture the audit-trail screen and the letter PDF into the re-performance workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled claim has an independent timing and content conclusion with the audit trail and letter captured.

testing.step: Re-test the prudence files against the published standard
actions: Pull each sampled fiduciary decision file and score it against the approved prudence-file standard without reading the auditor's conclusion.
Check the data relied on carries a date at or before the decision date — post-hoc data is reconstruction, not process.
Confirm the committee minutes and the materials the committee received are both present and consistent.
Record any file the audit passed that fails your read as a review exception against the audit itself.
testing.done: each sampled prudence file has an independent counsel score, with dated source data and matching minutes confirmed.

testing.step: Verify the cybersecurity attribute testing against the EBSA best practices
actions: For each recordkeeper, confirm evidence exists for all twelve EBSA Cybersecurity Program Best Practices, not a subset, and that each artifact post-dates the prior plan year end.
Read the third-party control audit report and the penetration test summary and confirm findings rated high or critical have documented remediation.
Confirm the EBSA Online Security Tips were actually distributed to participants and capture the communication with its send date.
Flag any recordkeeper covered only by a self-attestation as a testing failure.
testing.done: all twelve EBSA best practices are evidenced per recordkeeper with dated third-party artifacts and confirmed participant distribution.

testing.step: Recompute deadline and severity maths across the deficiency log
actions: Recompute the report issue date against plan year end +120 days and log any overrun with the days late.
Recompute each remediation plan date against report date +30 days and each re-test date against +90 days.
Re-apply the severity rubric to every finding independently, including the automatic upgrade for repeat findings, and compare to the recorded grade.
Recompute exception rates per control and compare to the 5% threshold and the zero-tolerance controls.
testing.done: report, remediation and re-test deadlines plus every severity grade and exception rate are independently recomputed and agreed.

testing.step: Log review exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per review exception naming the control, the workpaper reference, what the audit concluded and what re-performance concluded.
Assign a root cause (population filter error, wrong regulatory clock applied, prudence standard not enforced, closure on assertion only) and an owner in Internal Audit.
Set a remediation date before the next plan year's scoping and require the test script to be corrected, not just the workpaper.
Carry every open review exception into the next annual quality review as a mandatory retest item.
testing.done: every review exception has an issue, root cause, an Internal Audit owner, a remediation date and a script-level correction commitment.

testing.step: Conclude the quality review, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the re-performance agreement rate and compare it to the 5% and zero-tolerance thresholds.
State the conclusion on the ERISA key-control programme — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — with workpaper references.
Have the reviewer, who performed none of the original testing and owns no tested control, sign the quality-review workpaper.
Report the conclusion and all open review exceptions to the Audit Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under Plan Year.
testing.done: a signed quality-review workpaper with agreement rate, stated conclusion and Audit Committee reporting date is filed.

Deadline reminders configured.value: Board portal tasks at plan year end +30 days (issue independence questionnaire), +60 days (engagement letter executed), +120 days (fieldwork start independence re-confirmation); a rotation alert fires in the engagement partner's fourth consecutive year

checklist.step: Confirm which plans need an IQPA audit this plan year
actions: For each plan, count participants with account balances at the beginning of the plan year from the recordkeeping system — this is the counting method for defined contribution plans that determines large-plan status.
Apply the 80-120 participant rule: a plan that filed as a small plan last year and has between 80 and 120 participants may continue filing as a small plan.
For welfare plans, apply the 100-participant test and the 29 CFR 2520.104-44 exemption for unfunded/insured plans.
Produce the audit-required schedule with plan number, EIN, participant count, counting basis and audit-required Y/N, and give it to the Audit Committee.
checklist.done: an audit-required schedule exists per plan with the participant count, the counting basis and the 80-120 rule applied.

checklist.step: Issue the independence questionnaire built on Interpretive Bulletin 75-9
actions: Send the candidate or incumbent firm a questionnaire covering each IB 75-9 disqualifier: any direct financial interest or material indirect financial interest in the plan or the plan sponsor; connection to the plan or sponsor as promoter, underwriter, investment adviser, voting trustee, director, officer or employee during the period covered or at the time of the opinion.
Ask specifically whether any partner, professional employee or their immediate family holds an account in the plan or is a participant in it.
Require the firm to answer per office and per network firm, not just for the engagement team.
Set a 15-business-day response deadline and record the issue and response dates on the board portal task.
checklist.done: a completed IB 75-9 questionnaire is on file covering every disqualifier, answered at firm and network level.

checklist.step: Obtain the firm's written independence letter addressed to the Audit Committee
actions: Require a letter, signed by the engagement partner, affirming independence with respect to the plan under ERISA §103(a)(3)(A), 29 CFR 2509.75-9 and AICPA ET §1.200 for the entire period covered by the financial statements and through the opinion date.
Require the letter to disclose all relationships between the firm, its network firms, the plan and the plan sponsor that may reasonably bear on independence.
Reject any letter that limits its scope to the engagement team, omits the period covered, or is signed by anyone other than the engagement partner.
File the executed letter to the engagement folder on the board portal before the engagement letter is signed.
checklist.done: a partner-signed independence letter covering the full financial-statement period and the opinion date is on file before engagement.

checklist.step: Verify the firm's licence, peer review and EBP audit-quality credentials
actions: Confirm the firm's licence to practise in the relevant state through that state board of accountancy's licensee lookup and record the licence number and expiry.

Obtain the firm's most recent peer review report and its acceptance letter; a report rated 'pass with deficiencies' or 'fail' must be escalated to the Audit Committee with the firm's remediation plan.

Confirm membership of the AICPA Employee Benefit Plan Audit Quality Center and how many ERISA plan audits the office performs annually — a firm doing a handful of plan audits is a documented risk factor.
Ask whether the firm has been the subject of an EBSA Office of the Chief Accountant referral or a DOL audit-quality finding, and record the answer.
checklist.done: licence, current peer review report with rating, EBPAQC membership and audit-volume and referral history are all documented.

checklist.step: Assemble the complete fee schedule for the firm and its network
actions: Run a vendor spend report for the audit firm and every network entity across the plan and the plan sponsor for the financial-statement period and the current year to date.
Split spend into audit, audit-related, tax and other services, naming each engagement and its billing owner.
Chase down invoices booked to project or consulting cost centres that do not name the firm in the vendor master — this is where unapproved services hide.
Give the Audit Committee the reconciled fee schedule alongside the independence letter.
checklist.done: a reconciled, category-split fee schedule covering the firm and all network entities is before the Audit Committee.

checklist.step: Pre-approve or refuse every non-audit service before it is performed
actions: Maintain the pre-approval schedule listing permitted service categories with dollar limits and the prohibited list — bookkeeping for the plan, plan actuarial services, internal audit outsourcing over the plan, plan management functions, investment adviser or broker-dealer services to the plan.
Route every proposed engagement through the schedule before work starts; approvals after the fact are exceptions, not approvals.
Record each approval in Audit Committee minutes with the service description, fee cap and the reasoning that the service does not impair independence.
Report actual fees against each pre-approval at every Audit Committee meeting.
checklist.done: every non-audit service has a dated pre-approval before performance, with fee cap and minuted independence reasoning.

checklist.step: Track engagement-partner tenure and enforce rotation
actions: Maintain a rotation register per plan: engagement partner name, first year on the engagement, consecutive years served, engagement quality reviewer name and their tenure.
Apply the 5-consecutive-year cap on the engagement partner and the engagement quality reviewer with a 5-year cooling-off period before return.
Fire an alert in the partner's fourth consecutive year so the successor can shadow the audit before taking over.
Where the firm proposes an exception, require it in writing with the firm's own safeguards and put it to the Audit Committee for a minuted decision.
checklist.done: the rotation register shows tenure per partner and reviewer, with a successor identified before the fifth consecutive year ends.

checklist.step: Test the firm and the plan for prohibited relationships in both directions
actions: Run the firm's partner and professional roster against the plan's participant listing to detect any firm professional participating in the plan.
Run the firm's roster against the sponsor's employee and director listings to detect any dual role as director, officer or employee during the covered period.
Check the plan's investment holdings and service-provider list for the audit firm or its affiliates acting as investment adviser, broker or promoter.
Log any hit as a potential IB 75-9 disqualification and refer it to General Counsel before the engagement proceeds.
checklist.done: roster, participant, director and service-provider cross-checks are complete with every hit referred to counsel.

checklist.step: Take the independence determination to the Audit Committee for decision
actions: Present the pack: audit-required schedule, IB 75-9 questionnaire, independence letter, licence and peer review evidence, fee schedule, rotation register and cross-check results.
Ask the committee to record an explicit determination that the accountant is independent within the meaning of ERISA §103(a)(3)(A) — a silent approval of the engagement is not a determination.
Record any relationship disclosed and the committee's reasoning on why it does not impair independence.
Capture the resolution appointing the firm for the named plan year and the plans covered.
checklist.done: minutes record an explicit ERISA §103(a)(3)(A) independence determination and the appointment resolution by plan and plan year.

checklist.step: Execute the engagement letter with the scope ERISA requires
actions: Confirm the letter names each plan and plan number, the plan year, and whether the audit is a full-scope audit or a §103(a)(3)(C) limited-scope engagement relying on a qualifying institution's certification.

For a §103(a)(3)(C) engagement, confirm the certifying institution is a bank, similar institution or insurance carrier regulated and supervised and subject to periodic examination — and that the certification is signed by an authorised officer.
Confirm the letter commits the firm to communicate reportable findings and to deliver the opinion in time for the Form 5500 due date.
Route for signature only after the independence determination is minuted, then store the executed letter against the plan record.
checklist.done: an executed engagement letter names the plans, plan year, audit scope and delivery date, signed after the independence determination.

checklist.step: Re-confirm independence at fieldwork start and on any new service
actions: Within 30 days of fieldwork start, ask the engagement partner to re-confirm in writing that nothing has changed since the original letter.
Re-run the fee schedule for services billed since the letter and check each against the pre-approval schedule.
Where a new relationship or service has arisen, put it to the Audit Committee before the opinion date rather than after.
File the re-confirmation alongside the original letter in the engagement folder.
checklist.done: a dated written re-confirmation exists within 30 days of fieldwork start with an updated fee-versus-pre-approval check.

checklist.step: Log and dispose of any independence impairment
actions: Raise an issue naming the impairing fact, when it arose, which periods of the financial statements it touches and which plans are affected.
Ask General Counsel whether the impairment is curable (divest the interest, resign the role, unwind the service) or fatal to the engagement.
Where fatal, put to the Audit Committee the options: re-audit by an independent firm before the Form 5500 is filed, or file and correct — and record the decision and reasoning.
Track the issue to closure with the cure evidence or the replacement engagement letter attached.
checklist.done: every impairment has an issue with periods affected, a counsel curability opinion and a minuted Audit Committee disposition.

checklist.step: Receive and read the auditor's required communications
actions: Obtain the auditor's communication of significant findings: significant accounting practices, difficulties encountered, uncorrected misstatements and disagreements with management.

Obtain the written communication of internal control deficiencies (the management letter) and any reportable finding under ERISA-specific audit standards, including instances of non-compliance the auditor identified.
Route each finding to a named owner with a remediation date and load it into the deficiency log alongside internal audit findings.
Confirm the auditor's independence representation is repeated in these communications.
checklist.done: the auditor's findings and management letter are received, owner-assigned with dates, and the independence representation is repeated.

checklist.step: Evaluate the firm annually and decide on reappointment or tender
actions: Score the firm on plan-audit expertise, staffing continuity, timeliness against the Form 5500 deadline, quality of findings and fee competitiveness.
Collect feedback from the Controller, the Retirement Operations Administrator and the recordkeeper on the conduct of fieldwork.
Put reappointment, tender or replacement to the Audit Committee with the rotation register and the peer review rating alongside.
Record the decision and the reasoning in minutes so the appointment itself evidences a prudent §404(a)(1)(B) process.
checklist.done: a scored annual evaluation and a minuted reappointment, tender or replacement decision exist for each engagement.

checklist.step: File the engagement independence evidence for the retention period
actions: Move the engagement folder — questionnaire, independence letter, re-confirmation, licence and peer review evidence, fee schedule, pre-approvals, rotation register and minutes — into the evidence repository under Plan Year / Plan Number.
Apply the six-years-from-Form-5500-filing retention label required by ERISA §107.
Confirm the record is retrievable by plan number, EIN, audit firm name and engagement partner name.
Screen against legal holds so no engagement file under an open EBSA enquiry is purged on schedule.
checklist.done: the engagement independence file is retained under §107, indexed by firm and partner, and screened for legal hold.

testing.step: Build the population of engagements and firm-related spend
actions: List every plan requiring an audit for the plan year from the Controller's audit-required schedule and independently recount participants with account balances at plan year start.
Extract all vendor spend for the audit firm and every network entity across the plan and sponsor for the covered period, from the vendor master and from free-text invoice descriptions.
Add every executed engagement letter from the contract lifecycle management repository so an engagement without spend is not missed.
Sign the population as complete with extraction date, filters and row counts.
testing.done: a signed population lists every audit-required plan, every engagement letter and all firm and network spend for the period.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the filed Form 5500 accountant information
actions: For each plan, open the filed Form 5500 Schedule H and read the accountant's name, EIN and opinion type reported.
Compare to the engagement letters and the Audit Committee appointment resolutions and list any plan where the reported accountant differs.
Confirm every plan the schedule says needed an audit actually has an attached accountant's report in the filing.
Clear all differences before sampling — a mismatch here is itself a finding, not a data issue.
testing.done: the accountant named on every filed Schedule H reconciles to an appointment resolution and an executed engagement letter.

testing.step: Select the test scope and document it
actions: Take 100% of engagements — the obligation is per engagement and the population is small enough that sampling is not defensible.
Within firm spend, take 100% of non-audit engagements and 25 invoices by seeded random draw from routine audit billings.
Record the seed, population size and selection date so the invoice draw can be reproduced.
Note the performer of each independence determination so segregation from the reviewer can be evidenced.
testing.done: 100% engagement coverage plus a reproducible invoice draw is documented with performers identified.

testing.step: Re-perform the IB 75-9 independence determination from source
actions: Read 29 CFR 2509.75-9 and reach your own conclusion on each disclosed relationship before reading the Audit Committee's determination.
Confirm the independence letter covers the entire period of the financial statements and the opinion date, not just the engagement period.
Confirm the questionnaire was answered at firm and network level and that immediate-family and plan-participation questions were answered, not left blank.
Treat a determination reached with a blank or scope-limited answer on file as an exception, whatever the conclusion.
testing.done: each engagement has an independent counsel conclusion on IB 75-9 independence with period coverage confirmed.

testing.step: Test the non-audit fee schedule against the pre-approval record
actions: Match every non-audit invoice to a pre-approval entry on service description, fee cap and approval date.
Confirm the approval date pre-dates the earliest service date on the invoice — an approval dated after work started is an exception.
Recompute cumulative fees per service category against the pre-approved cap and flag any overrun.
Test every invoice for a prohibited service (plan bookkeeping, plan actuarial work, plan management, investment advice to the plan) regardless of whether it was approved.
testing.done: every non-audit invoice traces to a pre-dated pre-approval within its cap, with prohibited-service testing completed.

testing.step: Verify licence, peer review and rotation records independently
actions: Re-check the firm's licence status directly on the state board of accountancy licensee lookup as at the opinion date and capture the result.
Read the peer review report yourself and confirm the rating, the period covered and that the acceptance letter is present.
Recompute each engagement partner's consecutive years from the rotation register against the signed opinions on file, not the register's own count.
Flag any partner in a sixth consecutive year and any quality reviewer past the cap as a zero-tolerance fail.
testing.done: licence status at the opinion date, the peer review rating and recomputed partner tenure are independently verified.

testing.step: Trace the determination to minutes, engagement letter and opinion dates
actions: Open the Audit Committee minutes and confirm an explicit ERISA §103(a)(3)(A) independence determination is recorded, not merely an appointment.
Compare the determination date to the engagement letter execution date and to the fieldwork start date.
Confirm the 30-day post-fieldwork-start re-confirmation exists and is dated within the window.
Capture the minute extract, the letter signature page and the re-confirmation into the workpaper.
testing.done: each engagement shows a minuted determination pre-dating the engagement letter and a dated in-window re-confirmation.

testing.step: Recompute the audit-required determination and the deadline maths
actions: Recount participants with account balances at plan year start from the recordkeeping system and re-apply the 80-120 rule and the 100-participant welfare test.
Compare your audit-required conclusion to the Controller's schedule and log any plan that should have been audited but was not.
Recompute the Form 5500 due date as the last day of the 7th month after plan year end, plus the Form 5558 extension to October 15 where filed, and compare to the actual opinion delivery date.
Log every opinion delivered after the applicable due date with the days late.
testing.done: audit-required status and Form 5500 deadline maths are independently recomputed with any late opinion quantified.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception naming the plan, the firm, the impairing or missing fact and the financial-statement periods affected.
Assign a root cause (questionnaire not answered at network level, service engaged by a business unit without pre-approval, rotation register not maintained, determination never minuted) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, where independence was genuinely impaired, obtain counsel's written view on whether the Form 5500 must be amended with a re-audit.
Carry every open exception into the next engagement's independence pack as a mandatory check.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and a counsel view where independence was impaired.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report to the Audit Committee
actions: Compute the exception count against the zero-tolerance threshold — the metric here is a count, not a rate, because the population is engagements.
State the conclusion on the independence and rotation control — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — with workpaper references.
Have the reviewer, who neither negotiated the engagement nor prepared the independence pack, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Audit Committee at its next sitting, including any recommendation to tender the engagement, and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under Plan Year.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with exception count, stated conclusion and Audit Committee reporting date is filed in the repository.

In-scope systems.value: Plan trial balance and trust ledger source the Schedule H lines; the filing itself is prepared and transmitted through the EFAST2 IFILE/vendor software and the filing receipt is archived to the financial reporting repository

Compliance procedure documented.value: Form 5500 Annual Filing Procedure — participant count and large-plan determination, audit engagement, financial statement and supplemental schedule preparation, schedule-by-schedule preparer/reviewer assignment, EFAST2 signing and transmission, SAR distribution and DFVCP escalation for late filings

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Financial Officer and reviewed each year against the current Form 5500 Instructions before the cycle opens; changes to schedules or line items drive a procedure update before preparation starts

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Form 5500 due the last day of the 7th month after plan year end (July 31 for a calendar-year plan), extendable 2½ months to October 15 by filing Form 5558 on or before the original due date; the Summary Annual Report is due within 9 months of plan year end, or 2 months after the extended filing date

Deadline reminders configured.value: Close-calendar tasks at plan year end +60 days (trial balance final), +120 days (audit fieldwork start), +165 days (draft 5500 and opinion), +180 days (Form 5558 decision), plus a hard alert 10 business days before July 31 and October 15

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Filed Form 5500 with all schedules, the signed IQPA opinion and audited statements, the EFAST2 acknowledgement with its filing ID, the trial balance and reconciliations, and the SAR distribution proof retained six years from the filing date per ERISA §107

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: A filing accepted without the accountant's report, a late filing, or a schedule requiring amendment is logged with the plan number, the defect, the amended-filing date and any DFVCP submission and penalty paid recorded as the disposition

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Chief Financial Officer approves every amended Form 5500 and every Delinquent Filer Voluntary Compliance Program submission before it is transmitted

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every Form 5500 series filing made for the plan year across all plans, with their attached accountant's reports, supplemental schedules and EFAST2 acknowledgements, plus every plan on the register that made no filing

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance — a large-plan filing transmitted without the IQPA report is incomplete and treated by EBSA as not filed; any filing after the applicable due date, or any plan on the register with no filing, is a fail regardless of materiality

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual per plan; the test runs once per plan year at 100% coverage of filings, with an interim readiness review at plan year end +120 days

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have prepared any schedule, signed the filing, or maintained the trial balance for any plan tested

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual Form 5500 filing workpaper per plan (participant count support, trial balance, reconciliations, schedule tie-outs, opinion, EFAST2 acknowledgement, SAR proof) in the financial reporting repository, mirrored to the compliance evidence repository under Plan Year / Plan Number

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Filed 5500 package with the EFAST2 filing ID and acknowledgement, the signed accountant's report and the supplemental schedules of assets held and reportable transactions, producible to EBSA's Office of the Chief Accountant or an IRS Employee Plans examiner within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Controller answers EBSA filing-deficiency notices and IRS Form 5500 correspondence; General Counsel clears any DFVCP submission and any response admitting a late or incomplete filing before it is sent

checklist.step: Determine large-plan status and lock the filing scope
actions: Run the participant count as at the first day of the plan year: for defined contribution plans count participants with account balances; for defined benefit and welfare plans count eligible participants including terminated vested and beneficiaries receiving benefits.
Apply the 80-120 rule from the Form 5500 Instructions — a plan that filed as a small plan last year and has 80 to 120 participants may keep filing as a small plan.
Produce the filing-scope schedule: plan number, EIN, plan year end, participant count, small/large status, audit required Y/N, and the schedules each plan must file.
Circulate to the Controller and the engaged IQPA and freeze the scope before audit fieldwork is booked.
checklist.done: a frozen filing-scope schedule states counts, small/large status, audit requirement and required schedules per plan.

checklist.step: Close the plan trial balance and reconcile to the trustee and custodian
actions: Post all plan-year contributions, distributions, transfers, investment income and plan expenses and close the plan ledger by plan year end +60 days.
Agree total net assets available for benefits to the trustee statement and the custodian's year-end holdings report to the dollar; investigate any difference over $1,000 in writing.
Reconcile contributions receivable to the payroll remittance file and benefit payments to the 1099-R distribution file.
Sign the trial balance and hand the reconciliations to the IQPA as prepared-by-client items.
checklist.done: a signed plan trial balance agrees to trustee and custodian statements with contribution and distribution reconciliations attached.

checklist.step: Prepare the plan financial statements and the ERISA supplemental schedules
actions: Draft the statement of net assets available for benefits and the statement of changes, with the notes required for plan description, investment valuation, tax status and party-in-interest transactions.

Prepare Schedule H line 4i Schedule of Assets (Held at End of Year) with identity of issue, description, cost and current value, and Schedule of Assets (Acquired and Disposed of Within the Year) where applicable.
Prepare the Schedule of Reportable Transactions (Schedule H line 4j) using the 5%-of-plan-assets threshold measured at the beginning of the plan year.
Prepare Schedule G Part III for any non-exempt party-in-interest transaction, and confirm each is also reported on Form 5330 with the excise tax paid.
checklist.done: draft financial statements plus the assets-held, assets-disposed, reportable-transaction and Schedule G schedules are prepared and cross-footed.

checklist.step: Deliver the audit request list and support the IQPA through fieldwork
actions: Deliver the prepared-by-client list to the IQPA by plan year end +120 days: trial balance, reconciliations, plan document and amendments, SOC 1 reports, participant data extract, contribution register and distribution register.

For a 29 CFR 2520.103-8 limited-scope engagement, obtain the certification from the qualifying bank, similar institution or insurance carrier, signed by an authorised officer, certifying both completeness and accuracy of the investment information.
Track auditor open items daily and clear each within 3 business days so fieldwork does not slip past the filing runway.
Sign the management representation letter only after every uncorrected misstatement listed in it has been reviewed with the Chief Financial Officer.
checklist.done: fieldwork completes with all requests cleared, a valid certification where limited scope is used, and a signed representation letter.

checklist.step: Obtain the accountant's report in the correct form for the engagement
actions: Receive the signed accountant's report and check it names the plan and plan number, states the plan year audited, and is dated on or after the representation letter.

For a §103(a)(3)(C) engagement, confirm the report is in the ERISA-section-103(a)(3)(C) form — not a disclaimer of opinion — and that it includes the two-part opinion on the financial statements and on whether the information not covered by the certification is fairly stated.
Read the report for any modification, going-concern paragraph or emphasis of matter and brief the Audit Committee on it before filing.
Confirm the audited financial statements attached to the report are the exact ones prepared, page for page.
checklist.done: a signed, correctly-formed accountant's report names the plan and plan year and attaches the exact audited statements.

checklist.step: Prepare Form 5500 and the required schedules line by line
actions: Complete Form 5500 Part I and II: plan name, plan number, sponsor EIN, plan year dates, plan characteristic codes, and participant counts on lines 5 and 6 agreeing to the filing-scope schedule.

Complete Schedule H from the trial balance, tying line 1l total assets and line 2 income and expenses to the audited statements to the dollar, and answering the line 4 compliance questions including 4a late participant contributions.

Complete Schedule A for every insurance contract from the carrier's Schedule A data, Schedule C for service providers receiving $5,000 or more, Schedule D for master trust and DFE interests, and Schedule R for distributions and minimum funding.
Where line 4a reports late participant contributions, attach the schedule of delinquent participant contributions and confirm lost earnings were funded.
checklist.done: every required schedule is complete with Schedule H tied to the audited statements to the dollar and line 4 questions answered.

checklist.step: Run the second-person review of the filing against the current instructions
actions: Open the current plan year's Form 5500 Instructions — not the prior year's — and review each completed line against the instruction text.
Tie participant counts on lines 5 and 6 back to the recordkeeping extract and the filing-scope schedule.
Check every 'Yes' answer in Schedule H line 4 has the attachment the instructions require, and every plan characteristic code is valid for the plan type.
Sign the review checklist per schedule; an unsigned schedule does not go into the transmission.
checklist.done: each schedule carries a signed second-person review against the current-year instructions with all required attachments present.

checklist.step: Decide on and file the Form 5558 extension before the original due date
actions: By plan year end +180 days, assess whether the audit and the filing package will be complete by the last day of the 7th month after plan year end.
Where the runway is short, prepare Form 5558 Application for Extension of Time and file it with the IRS on or before the original due date — filed late, the extension is void and the filing is late.
Record the extension per plan and reset the calendar to the extended date, 2½ months later (October 15 for a calendar-year plan).
Confirm no plan relies on an extension that was never actually filed.
checklist.done: each plan has either a runway confirmation or a Form 5558 filed on or before the original due date, with the calendar reset.

checklist.step: Attach the accountant's report and validate the filing before transmission
actions: Attach the signed accountant's report and audited statements to Schedule H as a PDF attachment of type 'Accountant's Opinion' — a large-plan filing without it is treated as incomplete and rejected.
Attach the schedule of delinquent participant contributions and any other required attachment with the exact attachment types the instructions name.
Run the EFAST2 validation in the filing software and clear every error and every warning, documenting the reason for any warning left standing.
Print the pre-transmission proof and circulate it to the Controller and the plan administrator for final read.
checklist.done: the opinion and all required attachments are attached with correct types and EFAST2 validation runs clean or with documented warnings.

checklist.step: Sign and transmit the filing through EFAST2
actions: Confirm the plan administrator holds a current EFAST2 electronic signature credential (filing signer user ID and PIN) and that the credential is not shared.

Have the plan administrator apply the electronic signature to the filing; where a service provider signs under the instructions' alternative option, confirm the written authorisation and that a paper copy with the manual signature is retained.
Transmit and wait for the acknowledgement, then read the filing status — Filing Received, Filing Error, or Filing Stopped — and act on anything other than a clean receipt the same day.
Record the EFAST2 filing ID, transmission date and status on the filing-scope schedule.
checklist.done: the filing is signed by an authorised signer, transmitted, and an EFAST2 acknowledgement with filing ID and clean status is recorded.

checklist.step: Distribute the Summary Annual Report to participants and beneficiaries
actions: Produce the SAR on the format prescribed by 29 CFR 2520.104b-10 with the plan-year figures taken from the filed Schedule H.
Distribute within 9 months after plan year end, or within 2 months after the extended filing date where Form 5558 was filed, to every participant covered and every beneficiary receiving benefits.

Use a method reasonably calculated to ensure actual receipt — first-class mail, hand delivery, or electronic delivery meeting 29 CFR 2520.104b-31 or the 2520.104b-1(c) safe harbour, and record the method per population.
Retain the distribution list, the mailing or transmission log and a specimen copy as proof.
checklist.done: the SAR is distributed inside the 9-month or extended window with a retained distribution list, delivery method and specimen.

checklist.step: Route the auditor's communications to the Audit Committee
actions: Collect the auditor's communication of significant findings and the management letter of internal control deficiencies and reportable findings.
Present them to the Audit Committee with management's response, an owner and a remediation date for each point.
Load each point into the deficiency log so it is retested with the ERISA key-control programme.
Record the committee's acceptance of the audited financial statements in minutes before the filing is transmitted where the committee's approval is required.
checklist.done: auditor communications are before the Audit Committee with owners and dates, and acceptance is minuted.

checklist.step: Deal with a late, rejected or defective filing without delay
actions: Where EFAST2 returns Filing Error or Filing Stopped, correct and re-transmit the same day and record both the original and corrected filing IDs.
