Where a filing is or will be late, prepare a Delinquent Filer Voluntary Compliance Program submission through the DFVCP online calculator and payment system before EBSA issues a notice — DFVCP is unavailable once a notice of failure to file arrives.
Compute the DFVCP penalty per plan and per year using the calculator's per-filing and per-plan caps and get Chief Financial Officer approval before paying.
Where a filed return is later found wrong, file an amended Form 5500 marking the amended-return box and attach an explanation.
checklist.done: every rejected, late or defective filing has a same-cycle correction, a DFVCP submission where applicable and CFO-approved penalty payment.

checklist.step: Post the filing to the plan record and satisfy participant document requests
actions: File the transmitted 5500 package, EFAST2 acknowledgement, opinion and audited statements against the plan record and mark them available for participant requests.
Set the service standard for ERISA §104(b)(4) participant document requests at 30 days from written request, with the plan's copying-charge schedule attached.
Confirm the filing appears on the EFAST2 public disclosure site and that the accountant's report is visible on it.
Record the plan's latest annual report reference so the SPD's 'how to obtain the annual report' statement stays accurate.
checklist.done: the filing package is on the plan record, visible on EFAST2 public disclosure, and a 30-day §104(b)(4) request path is live.

checklist.step: Retain the filing evidence for the ERISA §107 period
actions: Move the complete filing workpaper — filing-scope schedule, trial balance, reconciliations, schedule tie-outs, opinion, acknowledgement, SAR proof — into the evidence repository under Plan Year / Plan Number.
Apply the six-years-from-filing-date retention label required by ERISA §107 and the longer ERISA §209 label to the participant data extract.
Confirm retrievability by plan number, EIN, plan year and EFAST2 filing ID.
Screen against legal holds before any scheduled purge.
checklist.done: the filing workpaper is retained under §107, indexed by filing ID and plan number, and screened for legal hold.

testing.step: Build the population of plans and filings for the plan year
actions: Take the ERISA plan register as the denominator and independently recount participants with account balances at plan year start from the recordkeeping system.
Search the EFAST2 filing database by sponsor EIN for every filing made for the plan year and record plan number, filing ID, receipt date and status.
List every plan on the register with no corresponding filing — that list is the highest-risk part of the test.
Sign the population as complete with extraction date, sources and row counts.
testing.done: a signed population pairs every register plan to a filing or an explicit no-filing exception.

testing.step: Reconcile Schedule H to the audited financial statements and the trust ledger
actions: For every large plan, agree Schedule H line 1l total assets and line 2 total income and expenses to the audited statement of net assets and statement of changes, to the dollar.
Agree the audited net assets to the trustee and custodian year-end statements and to the plan trial balance.
Trace the Schedule H line 4i assets-held schedule totals back to the custodian holdings report.
Record any difference in dollars — a rounding narrative is not an explanation.
testing.done: Schedule H, the audited statements, the trial balance and the custodian statements agree to the dollar for every large plan.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection
actions: Take 100% of large plans and 100% of plans with no filing, a late filing or an EFAST2 error status.
Add 10 small-plan filings by seeded random draw.
Within each sampled filing, select 25 Schedule H line 4i asset lines and 15 Schedule C service-provider rows for detail testing.
Record the seed, population sizes and selection date so the draw is reproducible.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers all large plans, all defective filings and a random small-plan draw with detail selections.

testing.step: Re-perform the large-plan audit-requirement determination
actions: Recount participants with account balances at the first day of the plan year directly from the recordkeeping extract and compare to the count on Form 5500 line 5/6.
Re-apply the 80-120 rule using the prior year's filing status and state your own small/large conclusion before reading the filing-scope schedule.
For welfare plans, re-apply the 100-participant test and check the 29 CFR 2520.104-44 unfunded/insured exemption where a filing claimed it.
Any plan you conclude was large that filed as small, with no audit attached, is a zero-tolerance fail.
testing.done: each sampled plan has an independent small/large conclusion agreed to the filed participant counts, or an exception raised.

testing.step: Verify the accountant's report is attached, signed and correctly formed
actions: Open the filing on the EFAST2 public disclosure site and confirm an attachment of type 'Accountant's Opinion' is present and opens.
Read the report and confirm it names the plan and plan number, states the plan year, is signed by the firm and is dated on or after the management representation letter.
Where a §103(a)(3)(C) limited-scope engagement was used, confirm the report is in the ERISA-section-103(a)(3)(C) form and that a signed certification from a qualifying institution is on file.
Treat a missing, unsigned or wrong-year report as a fail on the ground that EBSA treats such a filing as not filed.
testing.done: every large-plan filing has an attached, signed, correctly-formed report for the right plan and plan year.

testing.step: Test Schedule H line 4 answers and their required attachments
actions: For each sampled filing, check every Schedule H line 4 'Yes' answer against the attachment the current-year instructions require.
Where line 4a reports delinquent participant contributions, agree the amount to the remittance testing results and confirm lost earnings were funded and allocated.
Where line 4d or Schedule G reports a non-exempt party-in-interest transaction, confirm a Form 5330 was filed and the excise tax paid.
Independently re-answer line 4 from the underlying records and flag any answer that understates a known failure.
testing.done: every line 4 answer is independently re-derived, attachments are present, and delinquent contributions tie to remediation evidence.

testing.step: Trace the filing to its EFAST2 acknowledgement and signer authority
actions: Match the recorded EFAST2 filing ID to the acknowledgement and confirm the status is Filing Received rather than Error or Stopped.
Confirm the electronic signer held plan administrator authority on the transmission date by reference to the Benefits Committee appointment records.
Where a service provider signed under the alternative option, confirm the written authorisation and that a manually signed paper copy is retained.
Capture the acknowledgement screen into the workpaper.
testing.done: each filing traces to a received acknowledgement signed by a person with evidenced authority on the transmission date.

testing.step: Recompute the filing and SAR deadline maths
actions: Recompute the original due date as the last day of the 7th month after plan year end and compare to the acknowledgement date.
Where an extension was claimed, obtain the filed Form 5558 and confirm it was filed on or before the original due date; an unfiled or late 5558 makes the return late.
Recompute the extended date as the original due date plus 2½ months and compare to the acknowledgement date.
Recompute the SAR deadline as plan year end +9 months, or the extended filing date +2 months, and compare to the distribution log date, recording days late.
testing.done: original, extended, and SAR deadlines are recomputed per plan and every overrun is quantified in days.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception naming plan number, EIN, plan year, filing ID and the specific defect.
Assign a root cause (participant count method wrong, audit started too late, 5558 not filed, attachment type wrong, SAR list incomplete) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, for any late or incomplete filing, obtain a decision on a DFVCP submission and an amended return before EBSA issues a notice.
Carry every open exception into the next plan year's filing readiness review as a mandatory check.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and a documented DFVCP/amendment decision.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the exception count against the zero-tolerance thresholds for missing opinions, missing filings and late filings.
State the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — with the workpaper references behind it.
Have the reviewer, who prepared no schedule and signed no filing, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Audit Committee and the Chief Financial Officer at the next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under Plan Year.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with exception counts, a stated conclusion and a committee reporting date is filed in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Policy Forms Specialist owns the ERISA disclosure content built into group certificates, SPD wrappers, claim and appeal letter templates and fee disclosures; content changes are cleared by Regulatory Counsel before release

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — ERISA §§102 and 503 (29 U.S.C. §§1022, 1133), 29 CFR 2520.102-3 (SPD content), 29 CFR 2560.503-1(g) and (j) (adverse determination and appeal notice content), and 29 CFR 2550.408b-2(c) (covered service provider fee disclosure), re-read on eCFR at each form-change release

In-scope processes.value: Product and form change intake through to release for group welfare and retirement products that are ERISA plans — Group Long-Term Care, Group Health, Group Life, Group Disability and Retirement/401(k) — covering the certificate, the SPD or SPD wrapper, the claims-procedure section, adverse determination and appeal letter templates, and the 408(b)(2) fee disclosure

In-scope systems.value: Form inventory, certificate and SPD templates and the letter template library are versioned in the policy administration platform; approved source documents are held in the document management repository under form number and edition date

Compliance procedure documented.value: ERISA Disclosure Content Procedure — the mandatory-content matrix (one row per required SPD element in 29 CFR 2520.102-3 and per required notice element in 2560.503-1(g)/(j)), the form inventory standard, the counsel review gate and the SMM trigger rules for material modifications

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and Regulatory Counsel; re-approved annually and on any amendment to 29 CFR 2560.503-1 or a new EBSA disclosure rule

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per change — the SPD must reach participants within 90 days after coverage begins and within 120 days after a plan becomes subject to ERISA; a Summary of Material Modifications is due within 210 days after the plan year in which the change was adopted, or 60 days for a material reduction in group health services; templates must be live before the change's effective date

Deadline reminders configured.value: Release-calendar alerts at T-60 (content matrix complete), T-45 (counsel cleared), T-30 (templates configured and tested) and T-0 against the change effective date, plus SMM tasks dated from plan-year end + 210 days for every adopted amendment

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Form inventory with edition dates, the completed content matrix, counsel clearance memos, specimen certificates, SPDs and letter templates retained six years from the Form 5500 filing date per ERISA §107, and for the life of any benefit claim under ERISA §209

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: A template released without a mandatory element — most commonly the ERISA §502(a) civil-action statement in an adverse determination letter — is logged with the affected form numbers, the populations that received the deficient version, the re-issue date and any remediation of claims decided on it

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Regulatory Counsel signs off every corrected disclosure template and decides whether claims decided under a deficient notice must be re-opened because 29 CFR 2560.503-1(l) deems remedies exhausted

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every ERISA-plan form, certificate, SPD, SPD wrapper, claims-procedure section, adverse determination template, appeal decision template and 408(b)(2) disclosure released or amended in the period, by form number and edition date

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on the mandatory elements — a missing §502(a) rights statement, a missing appeal-rights description, a missing plan-provision citation, or an SPD without the claims procedure fails the release outright and blocks it

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per change; the content test runs on 100% of releases at the pre-release gate, with a full re-read of the in-force form inventory annually

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have drafted or configured any sampled template or SPD section

Evidence location for test results.value: Per-release disclosure workpaper (content matrix, redlines, counsel clearance, specimen output, configuration screenshots) in the compliance evidence repository indexed by form number and edition date

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Form inventory with edition dates, specimen SPD and letter templates, and the content matrix showing each 29 CFR 2520.102-3 and 2560.503-1(g) element mapped to its location in the document — producible to EBSA or to a state market conduct examiner within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Head of Compliance owns EBSA and market conduct enquiries on disclosure content; Regulatory Counsel clears any response and any participant re-notification before it goes out

checklist.step: Take in the product or form change and classify it as ERISA-relevant
actions: Open the change record and record product, line of business, affected form numbers, target effective date and whether the coverage is offered through an employer plan.

Ask the Insurance Product Manager whether the product is sold to ERISA plan sponsors — group LTC, group health, group life, group disability and 401(k) are in scope; true individual and voluntary employee-pay-all arrangements meeting 29 CFR 2510.3-1(j) are not.

Where the safe harbour is claimed, record each of the four 2510.3-1(j) conditions and how the arrangement meets them — no employer contributions, completely voluntary participation, no employer endorsement, no employer consideration.
Tag the change record ERISA-in-scope or out-of-scope with the reason and route in-scope changes to the disclosure gate.
checklist.done: the change record carries an ERISA in/out call with the 2510.3-1(j) conditions evidenced where the safe harbour is claimed.

checklist.step: Refresh the form inventory for every document the change touches
actions: List every artifact affected: master group policy, certificate of coverage, SPD or SPD wrapper, enrolment material, claim form, adverse determination letter, appeal decision letter, fee disclosure.
Record for each the form number and edition date exactly as printed in the footer, the current in-force version and the states or plan sponsors it is used with.
Mark which artifacts serve as the SPD — for many group products the certificate plus a wrapper is the SPD, and that call determines which content rules apply.
Publish the refreshed inventory to the change record so nothing is amended off-inventory.
checklist.done: the inventory names every affected artifact with form number, edition date and its SPD role.

checklist.step: Build the mandatory-content matrix from 29 CFR 2520.102-3
actions: Create one row per required SPD element: plan name and sponsor name, EIN and plan number, plan administrator name/address/phone, agent for service of legal process, type of plan and administration, eligibility and participation rules, description of benefits, circumstances causing loss or denial of benefits, source of contributions and funding, plan year end, claims procedures, amendment and termination rights, and the ERISA rights statement.
For each row, record where in the certificate or wrapper the element appears, by section heading and page.

Include the model ERISA rights statement wording from 29 CFR 2520.102-3(t) and check it names the right to obtain plan documents, the right to a §104(b)(4) copy of the annual report, and the EBSA contact details.
Flag any element with no home in the document set — that is a build item, not a wording preference.
checklist.done: every 2520.102-3 element has a matrix row pointing to a named section and page, or a raised build item.

checklist.step: Write the claims-procedure section against 29 CFR 2560.503-1
actions: State the claim filing procedure, where and how claims are submitted, and who decides them.

State the decision timeframes for the plan type: group health post-service 30 days, pre-service 15 days, urgent care 72 hours; disability 45 days with two 30-day extensions; group LTC and other welfare claims 90 days with a 90-day extension; pension claims 90 days with a 90-day extension.
State the appeal timeframes: at least 180 days for the claimant to appeal a group health or disability denial, 60 days for other plans, and the plan's own decision windows on appeal.
State the claimant's right to bring a civil action under ERISA §502(a) following an adverse determination on review, and where external review applies, describe it.
checklist.done: the claims-procedure section carries the plan-type-specific clocks, appeal rights and the §502(a) civil-action statement.

checklist.step: Build the adverse determination letter template to the (g) content list
actions: Include each 29 CFR 2560.503-1(g)(1) element as a discrete merge block: the specific reason for the determination, reference to the specific plan provisions relied on, a description of any additional material or information necessary and why, and a description of the review procedures and time limits including the §502(a) right.
Where an internal rule, guideline, protocol or medical-necessity criterion was relied on, include either the rule itself or a statement that it is available free on request.

For disability claims add the (g)(1)(vii) blocks: discussion of the decision including disagreement with treating-provider or vocational-expert views and with any Social Security disability determination, and the internal rules or the statement that none exist.
Lock the mandatory blocks so a user cannot delete them when composing a letter.
checklist.done: the template renders every (g) element as a locked block, with the disability-specific blocks present on disability templates.

checklist.step: Build the appeal decision template to the (j) content list
actions: Include the (j) elements: specific reason, plan provisions relied on, a statement that the claimant is entitled to receive on request and free of charge reasonable access to and copies of all documents relevant to the claim, and a statement of the right to bring a §502(a) action.
Include the statement about any voluntary appeal level and the fact that it is voluntary, where the plan offers one.

For disability appeals, include the pre-decision notice mechanic — new evidence or rationale must be given to the claimant free of charge and as soon as possible in advance of the deadline, with a reasonable chance to respond.
Add the applicable contractual limitations period and the date on which it expires, which the (j)(4)(ii) disability rules require.
checklist.done: the appeal template renders every (j) element and, on disability, the pre-decision notice and limitations-period statements.

checklist.step: Provide the notices in a culturally and linguistically appropriate manner where required
actions: Identify counties where 10% or more of the population is literate only in the same non-English language, using the county list EBSA and HHS publish for this purpose.

For claimants in those counties, add the one-sentence statement in the relevant language on how to access language services, and stand up oral language services including answering questions and providing assistance with filing claims and appeals.
Arrange written translation of the notice on request and record which languages are supported.
Confirm the address-based trigger logic runs off the claimant address in the claims platform, not the employer address.
checklist.done: the language-services statement, oral assistance and on-request translation are live and triggered off claimant county.

checklist.step: Build the 408(b)(2) fee disclosure content for covered services
actions: Where the insurer is a covered service provider to a plan, draft the 29 CFR 2550.408b-2(c)(1)(iv) disclosure: description of services, statement of fiduciary or registered-investment-adviser status where applicable, all direct compensation, all indirect compensation with its payer and the arrangement it relates to, and compensation for termination.
For recordkeeping services, include the reasonable and good-faith estimate of the cost of recordkeeping where it is provided without explicit cost, with the methodology stated.
Set the delivery rule: reasonably in advance of the contract being entered, extended or renewed, and within 60 days of the provider knowing of any change.
Route the draft to Regulatory Counsel and file the approved version against the product.
checklist.done: an approved 408(b)(2) disclosure exists per covered service arrangement with delivery timing rules configured.

checklist.step: Redline against the in-force edition and run the counsel clearance gate
actions: Compare the proposed certificate, SPD and letter templates to the in-force editions and produce a redline showing every content change.
Read each mandatory-content matrix row against the redlined document and mark it satisfied, changed or missing.
Write a clearance memo naming the form numbers, the new edition date, the regulatory basis for each change and any residual risk.
Refuse clearance where any zero-tolerance element is missing; the release does not proceed on a promise to fix it post-launch.
checklist.done: a counsel clearance memo exists naming form numbers and edition dates with every matrix row marked satisfied.

checklist.step: Assign the new edition dates and retire the superseded versions
actions: Set the new form number and edition date on every changed artifact and print it in the footer of every page.
Set the retirement date on the superseded edition and confirm the platform will not select it for new issues after that date.
Record on the inventory which in-force populations keep the old edition and which will receive the new one.
Store the approved PDF specimens in the document management repository under form number and edition date.
checklist.done: new editions are dated and printed, superseded editions are retired with a date, and specimens are stored by form number.

checklist.step: Trigger the SPD or SMM distribution the change requires
actions: Decide the vehicle: a restated SPD, or a Summary of Material Modifications describing the change in the same understandable style.
Apply the deadline — SMM within 210 days after the end of the plan year in which the modification was adopted, or within 60 days of adoption for a material reduction in covered group health services.
For new coverage, schedule SPD delivery within 90 days after coverage begins and, for a newly ERISA-covered plan, within 120 days after it becomes subject to ERISA.
Record the vehicle, the population, the scheduled date and the delivery method against the change record.
checklist.done: an SPD or SMM is scheduled with its statutory deadline, population and delivery method recorded per change.

checklist.step: Test-render every template before release
actions: Generate specimen output for each template in a test environment across the scenarios that change the content: denial for eligibility, denial for medical necessity, denial on appeal, disability denial with an SSA award on file, and a claimant in a language-services county.
Read each specimen against the mandatory-content matrix and confirm no block is suppressed by a merge rule or a page-break.
Check readability — the SPD must be written in a manner calculated to be understood by the average plan participant — and run a readability score on the changed sections.
Attach the specimens to the release record as the pre-release evidence.
checklist.done: specimen output for every scenario is generated, matrix-checked, readability-scored and attached to the release record.

checklist.step: Release the templates and confirm they are live
actions: Promote the approved templates on or before the change effective date and confirm the platform is selecting the new edition for new determinations.
Generate one live specimen after promotion and compare it to the approved specimen block for block.
Confirm the retired edition is no longer selectable and that in-flight claims continue on the edition in force when the claim was filed.
Record the promotion timestamp, the operator and the verification specimen in the release record.
checklist.done: the new edition is live and verified by a post-promotion specimen, with the retired edition blocked from new selection.

checklist.step: Log and remediate any deficient content already in the field
actions: Raise an issue naming the form numbers and editions carrying the deficiency, the period they were in use and the participant populations that received them.
Quantify the affected determinations by pulling every letter issued on the deficient template within the period from the claims platform.
Ask Regulatory Counsel whether affected claimants must be re-notified and whether appeal windows restart because 29 CFR 2560.503-1(l) deems remedies exhausted where the procedure was not followed.
Track re-issue and re-notification to completion with a per-claimant log.
checklist.done: every deficient edition has an issue with affected populations quantified, a counsel decision on re-notification and a completion log.

checklist.step: Retain the disclosure evidence for the ERISA retention period
actions: File the content matrix, redlines, counsel clearance memo, approved specimens and release verification into the evidence repository indexed by form number and edition date.
Apply the six-years-from-Form-5500-filing label required by ERISA §107, and the ERISA §209 label to specimens that could be needed to determine a benefit.
Confirm retrievability by form number, edition date, plan number and effective-date range so the version in force on any past claim date can be produced.
Screen against legal holds before any purge.
checklist.done: every edition's disclosure evidence is retained, indexed by form number and edition date, and retrievable by claim date.

testing.step: Build the population of ERISA-relevant form and template releases
actions: Extract every form, certificate, SPD, wrapper and letter template with an edition date or promotion date inside the period, with form number, edition date and product.
Add template configuration releases from the change management record so a merge-rule change that alters notice content cannot hide behind an unchanged form number.
Cross-check against the product change backlog for ERISA-in-scope changes and list any change with no corresponding form release.
Sign the population as complete with extraction date, filters and row counts.
testing.done: a signed population lists every release with form number and edition date, reconciled to the ERISA-in-scope change backlog.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the form inventory and the live platform configuration
actions: Compare the population to the Policy Forms Specialist's form inventory and list any artifact in one but not the other.
Query the live template configuration for the editions currently selectable and confirm every retired edition is genuinely blocked.
Identify any live template with no corresponding counsel clearance memo — that is an unapproved document in production.
Clear every difference before sampling.
testing.done: population, inventory and live configuration reconcile, with every live template traced to a clearance memo.

testing.step: Draw the sample and document the selection
actions: Take 100% of adverse determination and appeal decision templates and 100% of SPDs and wrappers released in the period.
Add 15 certificates and enrolment artifacts by seeded random draw.
Add 25 letters actually issued to claimants in the period, stratified across group LTC, disability, health and life.
Record the seed, population size and selection date so the draw is reproducible.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers all notice templates and SPDs plus a stratified draw of issued letters.

testing.step: Re-read each sampled SPD against 29 CFR 2520.102-3 element by element
actions: Work through the regulation's element list and locate each element in the document yourself, without using the preparer's content matrix.
Confirm the ERISA rights statement matches the substance of the 2520.102-3(t) model, including the §104(b)(4) document-request right and the EBSA contact details.
Confirm the claims procedure and appeal rights are in the SPD itself, not only in a separate booklet the participant has not been given.
Record every element you cannot find as an exception, naming the element and the document searched.
testing.done: each sampled SPD has an independent element-by-element result with any missing element named.

testing.step: Re-perform the (g) and (j) content test on issued letters, not just templates
actions: Open each of the 25 sampled issued letters in the claims platform as the claimant received them, including any suppressed or truncated blocks.
Score each against the 29 CFR 2560.503-1(g) or (j) element list independently, and for disability letters against the (g)(1)(vii) additional elements.
Confirm the §502(a) civil-action statement is present on every adverse determination on review — its absence is a zero-tolerance fail.
Compare template-level compliance to issued-letter compliance; a compliant template that renders a non-compliant letter is a configuration failure, not a documentation gap.
testing.done: every sampled issued letter is scored element by element, with template-versus-rendered differences identified.

testing.step: Test the language-services trigger on a live population
actions: Pull claimant addresses for the period and identify claimants in counties on the published 10%-non-English-literacy list.
For each, check the issued notice carried the language-services statement in the relevant language.
Call the published oral language services number and confirm a person can answer questions and assist with filing an appeal in that language.
Log any claimant in a triggering county who received an English-only notice as an exception.
testing.done: the county trigger is tested against live claimant addresses and the oral services line is confirmed answered in-language.

testing.step: Trace each sampled release to its clearance, specimen and go-live evidence
actions: For each sampled release, locate the counsel clearance memo and confirm it names the exact form number and edition date released.
Confirm the clearance date pre-dates the promotion timestamp; a clearance obtained after go-live is an exception.
Compare the approved specimen to the post-promotion verification specimen block for block.
Capture the promotion record and both specimens into the workpaper.
testing.done: each release traces to a pre-dated clearance memo and matching approved and post-promotion specimens.

testing.step: Recompute the SPD and SMM distribution deadlines
actions: For each new coverage in the period, recompute the SPD deadline as coverage start +90 days and compare to the distribution log date.
For each adopted modification, recompute the SMM deadline as plan year end +210 days, or adoption +60 days for a material reduction in group health services, and compare to the actual date.
Where a plan first became subject to ERISA in the period, recompute the 120-day SPD deadline.
Record every overrun in days and the participant headcount affected.
testing.done: SPD and SMM deadlines are recomputed per event with every overrun quantified in days and headcount.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception naming the form number, edition date, the missing element and the affected population.
Assign a root cause (matrix row never built, merge rule suppressed the block, clearance bypassed for a deadline, county list not refreshed) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and obtain Regulatory Counsel's decision on whether affected claimants must be re-notified and appeal windows restarted under 29 CFR 2560.503-1(l).
Carry every open exception into the next release gate as a mandatory pre-release check.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and a counsel decision on claimant re-notification.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the element-level exception rate for templates and separately for issued letters, against the zero-tolerance mandatory elements.
State the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — with workpaper references.
Have the reviewer, who drafted and configured none of the sampled templates, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting, including any re-notification programme, and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository indexed by form number.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with template and issued-letter exception rates, a stated conclusion and a committee reporting date is filed.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Policy Administration Operations Lead owns generation and delivery of ERISA participant notices — endangered/critical status and funding-improvement or rehabilitation disclosures on pension plans, SPD/SMM delivery, and claim and appeal notices — with the notice log as the control record

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — ERISA §305 and §432 for multiemployer endangered/critical status certification and notice, ERISA §104(b)(1) with 29 CFR 2520.104b-2 (SPD delivery windows), 29 CFR 2560.503-1(f)(1) and (i)(1) (initial determination and appeal timeframes) and 29 CFR 2520.104b-1/104b-31 (delivery methods and the electronic safe harbours), re-read at each annual procedure review

In-scope processes.value: Event-driven notice generation and delivery across administered ERISA plans: actuarial zone certification and the resulting endangered/critical status notice, funding improvement and rehabilitation plan disclosures, SPD delivery on new coverage and on a participant first receiving benefits, SMMs, and every claim and appeal determination notice

In-scope systems.value: Notice triggers, template selection, print/e-delivery hand-off and the notice log with per-participant delivery status live in the policy administration platform; claim-driven notices originate in the claims platform and post back to the same log

Compliance procedure documented.value: ERISA Notice Generation & Delivery Procedure — trigger-to-notice map (event, statutory deadline, recipient set, template, delivery method), the notice log standard, undeliverable-mail handling, and the escalation path when a statutory clock is at risk

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and the Chief Operating Officer; re-approved annually and on any change to the plan's claims procedure or to a statutory notice deadline

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Zone certification by the plan actuary within 90 days of the start of the plan year; endangered/critical status notice to participants, beneficiaries, the bargaining parties, the DOL and PBGC within 30 days of certification; funding improvement or rehabilitation plan adopted within 240 days of certification; SPD within 90 days after coverage begins and within 90 days of a participant first receiving benefits; claim determinations within the plan-type clock in 29 CFR 2560.503-1(f) and appeals within (i)

Deadline reminders configured.value: Notice-queue alerts at 50% and 80% of every statutory clock, a daily aged-notice report to supervisors for anything within 5 days of its deadline, and calendar tasks dated from plan year start +90 (certification) and certification +30 (status notice) and +240 (funding plan)

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Notice log with per-recipient generation and delivery timestamps, specimen notices, mailing/e-delivery vendor confirmations, undeliverable-return handling and the actuary's zone certification retained six years from the Form 5500 filing date per ERISA §107 and for the life of any benefit claim per ERISA §209

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Every notice generated after its statutory deadline, or not generated at all, is logged with the recipient count, days late, the reason and the disposition — late notice issued, appeal window restarted, or regulator notified

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Head of Compliance signs off every late-notice remediation and any decision to restart a claimant's appeal window or re-issue to a whole population

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every notice-triggering event in the period: zone certifications, funding improvement or rehabilitation plan adoptions, new coverage effective dates, first benefit payments, plan amendments, and all claim determinations and appeal decisions across administered plans

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on statutory clocks — one endangered/critical notice outside the 30-day window, one SPD outside the 90-day window, or one claim determination outside the 2560.503-1(f) clock is a fail; delivery-method failures fail at more than 2% of the recipient population

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is event-driven; the test runs monthly on the prior month's triggering events at 100% coverage of statutory-notice events and a sample of claim notices, with a full annual look-back

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must sit outside Policy Administration Operations and must not have generated or released any sampled notice

Evidence location for test results.value: Monthly notice-timeliness workpaper (event population, notice log extract, delivery confirmations, exception schedule) in the compliance evidence repository indexed by plan number and event month

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Notice log export with event date, deadline, generation and delivery timestamps and recipient counts, plus specimen notices and the actuary's certification — producible to EBSA or PBGC within 5 business days of a request

Regulator response path.value: Head of Compliance owns EBSA and PBGC enquiries about notice delivery; Regulatory Counsel clears any admission of a missed statutory notice and any participant re-notification before it is issued

checklist.step: Maintain the trigger-to-notice map for every administered plan
actions: Build one row per notice type: triggering event, statutory citation, deadline in days, recipient set, template form number, delivery method and the system that fires the trigger.

Include the pension zone-status notices, funding improvement and rehabilitation plan disclosures, SPD on new coverage, SPD on first receiving benefits, SMM, and the claim and appeal determination notices for each plan type.
Have Regulatory Counsel confirm the deadline and recipient set on each row against the current statute and regulation.
Publish the map to Policy Administration Operations and the claims teams and re-confirm it annually.
checklist.done: a counsel-confirmed map exists with deadline, recipients, template and triggering system for every notice type.

checklist.step: Obtain the plan actuary's zone certification within 90 days of plan year start
actions: For each multiemployer or defined benefit plan administered, request the enrolled actuary's certification of funded status no later than the 90th day of the plan year.
Read the certification for the zone determination — endangered (yellow), seriously endangered (orange), critical (red) or critical and declining — and the projections behind it.
Confirm the actuary has filed the certification with the Secretary of the Treasury as ERISA §305(b)(3)(A) requires and record the filing date.
Log the certification date on the notice log; the 30-day notice clock runs from this date, not from when operations happened to see it.
checklist.done: a dated zone certification is on file within 90 days of plan year start with the zone recorded and the notice clock started.

checklist.step: Assemble the recipient set for a status notice
actions: Build the recipient list: all participants and beneficiaries, each employer contributing to the plan, and each employee organisation representing participants — plus the DOL and PBGC as statutory recipients.
Refresh addresses against the sponsor's payroll file and the national change-of-address service before extraction, and flag records with no current address.
Reconcile the recipient count to the participant count used in the actuarial certification and explain any difference.
Freeze the list with an extraction timestamp so the population sent can be proven later.
checklist.done: a frozen, address-refreshed recipient list covers participants, beneficiaries, contributing employers, bargaining parties, DOL and PBGC.

checklist.step: Generate the endangered or critical status notice within 30 days of certification
actions: Select the template matching the certified zone and populate the plan name, plan number, plan year, certified status and the date of certification.
Where the plan is in critical status, include the statement that adjustable benefits may be reduced and that the plan may not pay lump sums or other accelerated forms while in critical status.
Use the DOL model notice content for critical-status plans where it applies, and follow the notice content requirements in the applicable Treasury and DOL guidance for endangered-status plans.
Release the notice to print and e-delivery no later than day 25 after certification so the 30-day statutory delivery date is met with margin.
checklist.done: the correct-zone notice is generated with certification date and benefit-restriction language and released by day 25.

checklist.step: Deliver the notice by a method reasonably calculated to ensure actual receipt
actions: Send by first-class mail, hand delivery, or electronically where the recipient meets the 29 CFR 2520.104b-1(c) work-related-computer-access safe harbour or has consented, or the 2520.104b-31 notice-and-access rules for retirement plan disclosures are satisfied.
Do not rely on posting to an intranet alone — placement in a location where a participant might see it does not meet 29 CFR 2520.104b-1(b)(1).
Send the DOL and PBGC copies by the channel each specifies and keep the transmission receipt.
Load the mail vendor's confirmation file and the e-delivery bounce report back into the notice log within 2 business days of send.
checklist.done: every recipient class is delivered by a compliant method with vendor confirmations and bounce reports loaded to the log.

checklist.step: Handle undeliverable notices and address failures
actions: Work the returned-mail queue daily; for each return, run the address through the sponsor payroll file, the national change-of-address service and a commercial locator search.
Re-send within 10 business days of the return and record the second attempt on the notice log.

Where the participant remains unlocatable, apply the missing-participant search steps EBSA expects — certified mail, plan records, related-plan records, beneficiary contact and free electronic search — and document each step attempted.
Never close a recipient as delivered on the basis of a first-attempt send that came back.
checklist.done: every returned notice has a re-send within 10 business days or a documented missing-participant search trail.

checklist.step: Adopt and disclose the funding improvement or rehabilitation plan within 240 days
actions: Track the 240-day clock from the certification date for the plan sponsor to adopt a funding improvement plan (endangered) or rehabilitation plan (critical).
Assemble the schedules the plan sponsor must provide to the bargaining parties, including the default schedule where required, and record the date they were provided.
Provide the annual update of the funding improvement or rehabilitation plan and file it with the Form 5500 as the instructions require.
Log adoption date, schedule delivery date and annual update date on the notice log against the plan.
checklist.done: adoption within 240 days, schedule delivery to bargaining parties and the annual update are all dated on the notice log.

checklist.step: Fire the SPD delivery events on new coverage and first benefit payment
actions: Configure the trigger so a new participant's coverage effective date starts a 90-day SPD clock under ERISA §104(b)(1) and 29 CFR 2520.104b-2(a).
Configure a second trigger so a beneficiary first receiving benefits starts a 90-day SPD clock from the date benefits first begin.
Run a daily exception report of participants whose clock is past day 60 without a generated SPD and work it to zero.
Record the coverage or first-payment date, the SPD edition sent and the delivery date on the notice log per participant.
checklist.done: both 90-day SPD triggers fire automatically with a daily day-60 exception report worked to zero.

checklist.step: Run the claim and appeal notice clocks inside the claims platform
actions: Confirm the claim received date is stamped from actual receipt, not from when the file was assigned — 29 CFR 2560.503-1(f) runs from receipt.

Work each claim against its plan-type clock: 90 days for pension and non-disability welfare claims with a single 90-day extension, 45 days for disability with two 30-day extensions, 30/15/72-hour clocks for group health.

Issue any extension notice in writing before the original period expires, stating the special circumstances and the date a decision is expected — an extension taken without that notice is a missed deadline.
On appeal, apply the (i)(1) clocks and record the decision date; post every generated notice back to the central notice log.
checklist.done: every claim carries a receipt-date-based clock, written pre-expiry extension notices where used, and a logged determination.

checklist.step: Run the daily aged-notice report and escalate at-risk clocks
actions: Publish each morning a report of every open notice obligation with days elapsed, days remaining and the responsible queue.
Escalate anything inside 5 days of its statutory deadline to the supervisor by name, and anything inside 2 days to the Head of Compliance.
Reassign work off any queue whose oldest item is inside 5 days — capacity is the usual root cause of a missed statutory notice.
Record the escalation and the action taken against the notice-log row so the intervention is evidenced.
checklist.done: a daily aged report is published, with named escalations inside 5 days and recorded interventions on every at-risk row.

checklist.step: Maintain the notice log as the single control record
actions: Require every notice row to carry: plan number, recipient identifier, notice type, triggering event date, statutory deadline, generation timestamp, delivery method, delivery confirmation and status.
Reject rows with a delivery status of 'sent' but no vendor confirmation — an unconfirmed send is not evidence of delivery.
Reconcile the log monthly to the print vendor's job file and the e-delivery platform's send file and clear differences.
Lock the prior month's log after reconciliation so timestamps cannot be edited retrospectively.
checklist.done: the monthly log is complete, reconciled to vendor send files and locked against retrospective edits.

checklist.step: Log every late or missed notice and decide the remedy
actions: Raise an issue for each late or missing notice naming plan, notice type, recipient count, deadline, actual date and days late.
Assign a root cause (certification received late, address data stale, queue capacity, trigger not configured, vendor file failure) and an owner.
Ask Regulatory Counsel whether a late claim determination triggers 29 CFR 2560.503-1(l) deemed exhaustion so the claimant may proceed to court, and whether the appeal window must be reopened.
For a missed statutory pension notice, decide with counsel whether a self-report to EBSA or PBGC is required and record the decision.
checklist.done: every late or missed notice has an issue, days late, root cause, owner and a counsel decision on exhaustion or self-report.

checklist.step: Re-issue and re-notify where a notice was defective or missed
actions: Generate the corrected or omitted notice and send it by the compliant delivery method, with a covering statement explaining the date it should have been sent.
Where an appeal window was affected, state the new window explicitly and start the clock from the re-issue date.
Track each re-issue to a confirmed delivery and close the notice-log row only on that confirmation.
Report the re-issue population and completion rate to the Head of Compliance weekly until closed.
checklist.done: every re-issue is delivered and confirmed, with restarted appeal windows stated and weekly reporting to closure.

checklist.step: Report notice timeliness to the Compliance Committee monthly
actions: Publish the monthly metrics: on-time rate by notice type, count and days late of every breach, recipient counts affected and open re-issue population.
Show statutory-clock breaches separately from internal service-level misses — they are not the same risk.
Present trend against the prior six months and name the owner of any notice type below target for two consecutive months.
Record the committee's decisions and any required remediation in the minutes.
checklist.done: monthly metrics with statutory breaches shown separately are before the committee with named owners and minuted decisions.

checklist.step: Retain the notice evidence for the ERISA retention period
actions: Archive the monthly notice log, specimen notices, vendor confirmation files, bounce reports and returned-mail handling records under Plan Number / Event Month.
Apply the six-years-from-Form-5500-filing label required by ERISA §107 and the ERISA §209 label to records that evidence a benefit determination.
Confirm retrievability by participant identifier, notice type and event date so a single participant's full notice history can be produced.
Screen against legal holds for participants with open claims or litigation before any purge.
checklist.done: notice evidence is archived, retention-labelled, retrievable per participant and screened for legal hold.

testing.step: Build the population of notice-triggering events for the period
actions: Extract every triggering event in the period: zone certifications, funding plan adoptions, new coverage effective dates, first benefit payments, plan amendments, claim receipts and appeal receipts.
Take the events from the source systems that create them, not from the notice log — building the population from the log would only prove the log agrees with itself.
Record extraction date, filters and row counts per event type.
Sign the population as complete.
testing.done: a signed event population is built from source systems independently of the notice log, with counts per event type.

testing.step: Reconcile events to the notice log and to vendor send files
actions: Match every event to a notice-log row on plan, recipient and event date, and list unmatched events as automatic exceptions.
Reconcile notice-log send counts to the print vendor job file and the e-delivery platform send file, by notice type and month.
Investigate any log row marked delivered with no corresponding vendor record — that is an unsupported delivery claim.
Clear or document every difference before sampling.
testing.done: every event matches a log row and log deliveries reconcile to vendor send files, with unmatched items raised as exceptions.

testing.step: Draw the sample and document the selection
actions: Take 100% of statutory pension notices — zone certifications, status notices, funding plan disclosures — because the population is small and the clocks are absolute.
Take 40 claim and appeal determinations by seeded random draw, stratified across group LTC, disability, health, life and pension.
Take 25 SPD delivery events split between new coverage and first benefit payment.
Record the seed, population sizes and selection date so the sample is reproducible.
testing.done: a reproducible, stratified sample covers 100% of statutory pension notices plus claim and SPD draws.

testing.step: Recompute the 90-day certification and 30-day status notice clocks
actions: For each plan, recompute the certification deadline as plan year start +90 days and compare to the actuary's signed certification date.
Recompute the status notice deadline as certification date +30 days and compare to the delivery date, not the generation date.
Recompute the funding improvement or rehabilitation plan deadline as certification +240 days and compare to the adoption date.
Record every overrun in days and identify which recipient classes were affected.
testing.done: the 90-, 30- and 240-day clocks are recomputed per plan with overruns quantified in days and by recipient class.

testing.step: Re-perform the claim and appeal clocks from the claim file
actions: For each sampled claim, read the actual receipt evidence — the inbound document timestamp or postmark — rather than the system's assignment date, and recompute the deadline for the plan type.
Where an extension was taken, confirm a written extension notice was issued before the original period expired and that it stated the special circumstances and the expected decision date.
Compare the determination letter date and the delivery date to the recomputed deadline and record days late.
Capture the claim audit trail into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled claim has a receipt-based recomputed deadline, extension-notice verification and a days-late figure.

testing.step: Test the delivery method against the ERISA disclosure rules
actions: For each sampled recipient, identify the method used and test it against 29 CFR 2520.104b-1(b) — reasonably calculated to ensure actual receipt.

For electronic delivery, confirm either the work-related-computer-access safe harbour conditions, an affirmative consent on file, or compliance with the 2520.104b-31 notice-and-access rules including the initial paper notice of internet availability.
Reject intranet-posting-only delivery and count it as non-delivery.
Confirm returned mail was re-sent within 10 business days or escalated to a documented missing-participant search.
testing.done: each sampled delivery is tested against the disclosure rules with electronic-delivery conditions evidenced per recipient.

testing.step: Trace recipient completeness on a statutory notice population
actions: For one status notice, rebuild the recipient set independently from participant, beneficiary, contributing employer and bargaining-party records as at the certification date.
Compare your count to the sent count and identify every recipient omitted or added.
Confirm the DOL and PBGC copies were sent and that transmission receipts exist.
Treat an omitted recipient class as a fail regardless of how small the class is.
testing.done: the recipient set is independently rebuilt and reconciled, with DOL and PBGC transmission receipts verified.

testing.step: Verify the notice content matches the certified status and required language
actions: Read the issued specimen and confirm it states the correct certified zone, the plan year, and the certification date.
For critical-status plans, confirm the adjustable-benefit reduction and lump-sum restriction statements are present.
Confirm the notice is written in a manner reasonably expected to be understood by the average participant, as ERISA disclosure standards require.
Record any wording that overstates or understates the plan's status as an exception and refer it for re-issue.
testing.done: each sampled statutory notice is confirmed against the certified zone with all required restriction language present.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception naming plan, notice type, recipient count, deadline, actual date and days late.
Assign a root cause (certification handed over late, trigger not configured, stale address data, queue capacity, vendor file failure) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and obtain counsel's decision on deemed exhaustion under 29 CFR 2560.503-1(l) and on any EBSA or PBGC self-report.
Carry every open exception into the next month's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, days late, root cause, owner, remediation date and a counsel exhaustion/self-report decision.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the on-time rate by notice type and compare statutory-clock breaches to the zero-tolerance threshold and delivery failures to the 2% threshold.
State the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — with workpaper references.
Have the reviewer, who sits outside Policy Administration Operations and generated no sampled notice, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under Plan Number / Event Month.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with on-time rates by notice type, a stated conclusion and a committee reporting date is filed.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Business Systems Analyst owns the requirement-to-configuration trace for ERISA timing and content rules in the claims and policy administration platforms; the Head of IT owns delivery and Regulatory Counsel signs off the rule interpretation behind each configuration

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — 29 CFR 2560.503-1(f) and (i) for the determination and appeal clocks the system enforces, 2560.503-1(g) and (j) for the letter content it renders, 2560.503-1(l) for the consequence of not following the procedure, and 29 CFR 2520.104b-31 for the electronic delivery conditions the platform must satisfy; each cited clause is quoted in the requirement it drives

In-scope processes.value: Change intake through release for the ERISA rule set inside the claims platform and the policy administration platform: claim-receipt date-stamping, plan-type decision clocks, extension-notice gating, appeal clocks, letter template selection and merge logic, notice-log write-back and electronic-delivery eligibility

In-scope systems.value: Claims platform rule tables and correspondence engine, with the policy administration platform holding SPD/SMM triggers and the notice log; changes flow through the ITSM change record and the CI/CD pipeline

Compliance procedure documented.value: ERISA System Rules Configuration Standard — one requirement per regulatory clause with its quoted text, the configuration object that implements it, the test case that proves it, and the counsel sign-off; plus the regression pack that must pass before any release touching claims correspondence or clocks

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of IT and the Head of Compliance; the requirement set is re-approved by Regulatory Counsel on any amendment to 29 CFR 2560.503-1 and at each annual review

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per change — configuration must be live before the change effective date; where a regulatory amendment drives the change, the configuration must be live by the amendment's applicability date, and any interim manual control runs from the day the requirement is known until go-live

Deadline reminders configured.value: Release-calendar alerts at T-45 (requirements signed), T-30 (configuration complete in the test environment), T-14 (regression pack green), T-7 (counsel sign-off) and T-0 against the change effective date, tracked on the ITSM change record

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Requirement register with quoted regulatory text, configuration exports, test cases and results, regression evidence, counsel sign-off and the deployment record retained six years from the Form 5500 filing date per ERISA §107; production correspondence generated by the configuration retained per ERISA §209

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: A release that alters a clock or a notice template without a signed requirement, or a defect found in production affecting a statutory clock, is raised as a P1 change/incident with the affected claim population, the interim manual control and the fix release recorded as the disposition

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Head of Compliance signs off closure of any production defect that affected a statutory clock or a notice's mandatory content, only after the affected claim population has been identified and remediated

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every configuration change released in the period that touches ERISA clocks, correspondence templates, merge rules, delivery-method eligibility or notice-log write-back, plus the production determinations those changes governed

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance — a release that changes a statutory clock or removes a mandatory notice block without a signed requirement and a passing test case is a fail; regression pack must be 100% green, and any production defect touching a clock is automatically a significant deficiency

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per change; the control is tested on 100% of releases at the pre-deployment gate, with a quarterly re-verification of the live rule tables against the requirement register

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have written the configuration or the test case being verified, and cannot approve their own change record

Evidence location for test results.value: Per-release configuration workpaper (requirement register extract, configuration export, test cases and evidence, regression results, counsel sign-off, deployment record) attached to the ITSM change record and mirrored to the compliance evidence repository

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Requirement register showing each 29 CFR 2560.503-1 clause mapped to the configuration object and the passing test case, plus the deployment record — the artifact that answers a regulator asking how the system is made to honour the claims-procedure regulation

Regulator response path.value: Head of Compliance owns the regulator-facing explanation of system controls; the Head of IT supplies configuration and deployment evidence, and Regulatory Counsel clears any statement about periods when a clock was mis-enforced

checklist.step: Take in the change and identify which ERISA rules it touches
actions: Open the change record and capture the driver: a new product, a plan-document amendment, a regulatory amendment, or a defect fix.
Screen the change against the ERISA rule inventory — clocks, extension gating, letter content, delivery eligibility, notice-log write-back — and tick every area touched.
Where any area is touched, tag the change 'ERISA-controlled' so it cannot deploy without counsel sign-off and a regression run.
Name the accountable Business Systems Analyst and the Regulatory Counsel reviewer on the change record.
checklist.done: the change record is screened, tagged ERISA-controlled where applicable, and has a named analyst and counsel reviewer.

checklist.step: Write the requirements with the regulatory text quoted in each one
actions: Write one requirement per regulatory clause, quoting the operative text — for example 29 CFR 2560.503-1(f)(3): notification of a disability benefit determination not later than 45 days after receipt of the claim.
State the input the system reads (claim received timestamp, plan type, claim category), the computation, and the observable output (due date field, queue alert, letter block).
Write the negative requirement too: what the system must prevent — an extension recorded without a pre-expiry written notice, a letter released with a suppressed §502(a) block.
Have Regulatory Counsel sign each requirement before configuration starts; an unsigned requirement is not built.
checklist.done: every requirement quotes its clause, names input, computation and output, and carries a counsel signature before build.

checklist.step: Configure the plan-type decision clocks in the claims platform
actions: In the claims platform rule tables, set the decision clock per plan type and claim category: group health urgent 72 hours, pre-service 15 days, post-service 30 days; disability 45 days; pension and other welfare 90 days.
Set the clock start to the claim received timestamp captured at intake, and confirm it does not reset on reassignment, document upload or queue transfer.
Configure the extension rules: the permitted number and length per plan type, and a hard gate requiring the extension letter to be generated and dated before the original period expires.
Export the configured rule table and attach it to the change record as the configuration evidence.
checklist.done: clocks and extension gates are configured per plan type from the received timestamp, with the rule table exported to the change record.

checklist.step: Configure the appeal clocks and the claimant appeal window
actions: Set the claimant's appeal window at 180 days for group health and disability denials and 60 days for other plans, running from receipt of the adverse determination.
Set the plan's appeal decision clocks per 29 CFR 2560.503-1(i) and confirm the system does not treat a voluntary second-level appeal as if it were mandatory.

Configure the disability pre-decision mechanic: where new evidence or a new rationale is added on appeal, the system must force generation of the claimant notice and hold the decision until a response window has passed.
Configure the contractual limitations period field so the appeal decision letter can state the date it expires.
checklist.done: appeal windows, plan decision clocks, the pre-decision hold and the limitations-period field are configured and exported.

checklist.step: Configure template selection and lock the mandatory merge blocks
actions: Map each determination outcome and plan type to the correct letter template edition, and set effective-dated selection so an in-flight claim keeps the edition in force at filing.
Mark the 29 CFR 2560.503-1(g) and (j) blocks as mandatory in the correspondence engine so no user, merge rule or page-fit routine can suppress them.
Configure the conditional blocks — internal rule availability statement, disability SSA/treating-provider discussion, language-services statement driven by claimant county.
Export the template-to-outcome mapping and attach it to the change record.
checklist.done: template selection is effective-dated per outcome and plan type with mandatory blocks locked against suppression.

checklist.step: Configure electronic-delivery eligibility and the notice-log write-back
actions: Configure the delivery-method decision to check, per recipient, an affirmative e-delivery consent, the work-related-computer-access conditions, or 29 CFR 2520.104b-31 notice-and-access eligibility including the initial paper notice.
Default to first-class mail where none of the conditions is satisfied — never default to email because an address exists.
Configure the write-back so every generated notice posts to the notice log with generation timestamp, delivery method, vendor job id and confirmation status.
Configure the bounce and returned-mail feeds to update the log row rather than creating a parallel record.
checklist.done: delivery eligibility is evaluated per recipient with a mail default, and every notice writes back to a single log row.

checklist.step: Write the test cases directly from the signed requirements
actions: Create one test case per requirement, linked to it, with the input data, the expected due date or rendered block, and the pass criterion stated as a date or a literal string.
Include boundary cases: a claim received at 23:59, a deadline landing on a weekend or holiday, an extension requested on the last day, and a claimant in a language-services county.
Include negative cases: attempt to record an extension without a pre-expiry letter, attempt to release a letter with the §502(a) block deleted — both must be blocked by the system.
Have the Test Lead review coverage and confirm no signed requirement is without a test case.
checklist.done: every signed requirement has a linked test case with boundary and negative cases and Test Lead coverage confirmation.

checklist.step: Execute the tests in a production-like environment with real plan data shapes
actions: Load a test set that reproduces the live plan mix — group LTC, disability, health, life and pension — and the live template editions.
Execute each test case, capture the rendered letter PDF and the computed due-date field as evidence, and record pass or fail against the literal criterion.
Re-run every failure after the fix rather than accepting a developer's explanation of why it failed.
Attach the executed test evidence to the change record.
checklist.done: all test cases are executed with rendered-letter and due-date evidence attached and every failure re-run to pass.

checklist.step: Run the ERISA regression pack over the untouched rules
actions: Run the standing regression pack covering every ERISA clock and every mandatory notice block, not only the areas the change touched.
Compare rendered output byte-for-byte against the approved baselines and investigate any diff, including whitespace, in a mandatory block.
Require 100% green before the change proceeds; a known-failing test carried as accepted is not green.
Publish the regression report to the change record with the pipeline run id.
checklist.done: the full ERISA regression pack is 100% green with a published report and pipeline run id on the change record.

checklist.step: Obtain counsel sign-off on the configured behaviour, not the requirement alone
actions: Review the rendered specimen letters and the computed due dates from the executed tests against the regulation text.
Confirm the negative cases genuinely blocked — an untested prohibition is an assumption.
Sign the configuration for release, naming the requirement ids and the test run covered.
Withhold sign-off where any mandatory block is renderable as suppressed, whatever the delivery pressure.
checklist.done: counsel has signed the specific test run and requirement ids after reviewing rendered output and negative-case results.

checklist.step: Approve the change and deploy with a documented back-out
actions: Confirm the change record carries the signed requirements, the executed tests, the green regression report and counsel sign-off before CAB approval.
Record the deployment window, the implementer, the verification owner and the back-out plan with the configuration version to restore.
Deploy on or before the change effective date and record the deployment timestamp and build id.
Reject any emergency change that skips counsel sign-off on an ERISA-controlled area; use an interim manual control instead.
checklist.done: the change is CAB-approved with all gate evidence, deployed on time, and a versioned back-out plan is recorded.

checklist.step: Verify the configuration in production immediately after deployment
actions: Create a controlled test claim in production for each affected plan type and confirm the due date computes to the expected value.
Generate one determination letter per affected template and read it against the mandatory-block list.
Confirm the notice-log write-back created a row with the correct delivery method and vendor job id.
Record the verification results and back out the change the same shift if any check fails.
checklist.done: post-deployment verification confirms clocks, letter blocks and log write-back in production, or the change is backed out.

checklist.step: Run the interim manual control whenever configuration lags the requirement
actions: Where a regulatory change applies before the system can be configured, stand up a manual control from the applicability date: a daily worklist of affected claims with manually computed deadlines.
Name the operator and the reviewer and require a dated sign-off on each day's worklist.
Track the manual control on the risk register with the target automation date and report it monthly until retired.
Retire the manual control only after post-deployment verification passes.
checklist.done: any requirement-to-configuration gap is covered by a dated, signed daily manual control tracked to the automation date.

checklist.step: Handle production defects that affect a statutory clock or a notice block
actions: Raise a P1 incident naming the defect, the rule affected, and the date range the defective behaviour was live.
Query the affected claim population for the whole date range and quantify determinations decided on a wrong clock or a deficient letter.
Stand up the manual control immediately, fix and deploy under the normal gates, and hand the affected population to Compliance for re-notification decisions.
Record the incident, the population, the fix release and the remediation outcome as a single closure package.
checklist.done: every clock or content defect has a P1 incident, a quantified affected population, an interim control and a closed remediation package.

checklist.step: Re-verify the live rule tables against the requirement register quarterly
actions: Export the live clock rule table, template-to-outcome map and mandatory-block settings from production each quarter.
Compare line by line to the signed requirement register and investigate every difference, including changes made under emergency approvals.
Confirm no ERISA-controlled object was changed without a change record — an undocumented drift is a control failure whatever the behaviour.
File the exports and the comparison in the evidence repository with the ERISA §107 six-year retention label.
checklist.done: a quarterly production-to-register comparison is filed with every difference investigated and retention-labelled.

testing.step: Build the population of ERISA-controlled configuration changes
actions: Extract every change record deployed in the period against the claims platform and the policy administration platform, with implementer, deployment timestamp and build id.

Independently identify ERISA-controlled changes by searching the deployment diffs for clock rule tables, correspondence templates and delivery-eligibility objects, rather than relying on the ERISA tag.
List any change touching those objects that was not tagged ERISA-controlled — that gap is the highest-risk finding.
Sign the population as complete with extraction date and row counts.
testing.done: a signed population identifies ERISA-controlled changes from deployment diffs and lists every untagged change touching those objects.

testing.step: Reconcile deployed configuration to the signed requirement register
actions: Export the live clock rule table, template mapping and mandatory-block settings from production as at period end.
Compare each line to the signed requirement register and list objects in production with no signed requirement and requirements with no production object.
Trace every difference to a change record and confirm it went through CAB with counsel sign-off.
Clear or raise every difference before sampling.
testing.done: live configuration reconciles to the signed requirement register with every difference traced to an approved change record.

testing.step: Draw the sample and document the selection
actions: Take 100% of ERISA-controlled changes, 100% of emergency changes touching those objects and 100% of P1 defects affecting a clock or a notice block.
Add 20 production determinations by seeded random draw from claims decided after each sampled deployment.
Record the seed, population sizes and selection date so the draw is reproducible.
Note the configurer and the tester on each sampled change so segregation can be evidenced.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers all ERISA-controlled and emergency changes, all clock defects and a post-deployment claim draw.

testing.step: Re-perform the clock computation in the claims platform for sampled claims
actions: For each sampled production determination, read the claim received timestamp from the audit trail and independently compute the deadline for the plan type and claim category.
Compare your figure to the system-computed due-date field and treat any difference as a configuration exception.
Test whether reassignment, document upload or queue transfer moved the clock by inspecting the audit trail for due-date changes.
Capture the audit trail and the due-date field into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled claim has an independently computed deadline agreed to the system field with clock-reset behaviour tested.

testing.step: Attempt the negative cases in a controlled environment
actions: In a production-like environment, attempt to record an extension without generating the pre-expiry written notice and confirm the system blocks it.
Attempt to release a determination letter with the §502(a) rights block removed and confirm the correspondence engine refuses.
Attempt to select a retired template edition for a new determination and confirm it is unavailable.
Record each attempt, the system response and a screenshot; a prohibition that has never been attempted is unproven.
testing.done: every prohibition is actively attempted and evidenced as blocked, with screenshots in the workpaper.

testing.step: Verify test and regression evidence behind each sampled change
actions: For each sampled change, confirm every signed requirement has a linked test case and an executed result with rendered evidence attached.
Confirm the regression pipeline run linked to the change is 100% green and that its run id matches the one on the change record.
Check for tests marked skipped, quarantined or accepted-failing and treat any in an ERISA area as a gate failure.
Confirm the tester is not the configurer on any sampled change.
testing.done: each sampled change shows full requirement-to-test coverage, a matching green regression run and tester/configurer segregation.

testing.step: Trace counsel sign-off, CAB approval and deployment timing
actions: Confirm the counsel sign-off names the requirement ids and the test run actually deployed, not an earlier run.
Confirm the sign-off and CAB approval both pre-date the deployment timestamp.
