For emergency changes, confirm the retrospective counsel review happened within the standard's window and that an interim manual control ran meanwhile.
Capture the change record, sign-off and deployment log into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled change shows counsel sign-off and CAB approval pre-dating deployment, with emergency changes retrospectively reviewed.

testing.step: Recompute defect exposure windows and remediation coverage
actions: For each sampled clock or content defect, recompute the exposure window from the deploying build's timestamp to the fix build's timestamp.
Independently query the claim population decided inside that window and compare your count to the population Compliance remediated.
Recompute how many of those determinations breached a statutory clock or carried a deficient notice.
Log any determination inside the window that was never assessed for remediation.
testing.done: each defect's exposure window and affected population are independently recomputed and reconciled to the remediation population.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception naming the change id, the configuration object, the rule affected and the claim population exposed.
Assign a root cause (requirement never written, ERISA tag missed at intake, test case absent, emergency path abused, drift with no change record) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and require the fix at the standard level — the intake screen, the regression pack — not only the individual configuration.
Carry every open exception into the next quarterly production-to-register comparison as a mandatory check.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and a standard-level fix commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the exception count against the zero-tolerance gate thresholds and the clock-computation agreement rate on sampled claims.
State the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — with workpaper references.
Have the reviewer, who wrote no sampled configuration and authored no sampled test case, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Compliance Committee and the Head of IT at the next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with gate exception counts, clock agreement rate, a stated conclusion and a reporting date is filed.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Compliance Manager owns the ERISA training curriculum and the annual completion cycle; Learning & Development builds and deploys it and each functional leader owns completion for their team

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — curriculum content is written from ERISA §404(a)(1)(B) prudence, 29 CFR 2560.503-1 in full (claims procedures, timeframes, notice content and the (l) consequence of not following the procedure), 29 CFR 2578.1 on abandoned individual account plans, and the EBSA Cybersecurity Program Best Practices issued with Compliance Assistance Release 2021-01; each module footnotes the clause it teaches

In-scope processes.value: Annual role-based ERISA training for every employee whose work touches an ERISA plan: claims examiners and disability case managers, retirement recordkeeping and operations, benefits administration, plan financial reporting, correspondence and contact centre staff, IT staff configuring plan systems, and the Benefits Committee members acting as fiduciaries

In-scope systems.value: Curricula, assignments, assessments and completion records live in the LMS, driven by an HRIS feed of job codes so new joiners and movers are auto-assigned

Compliance procedure documented.value: ERISA Training Standard — role-to-curriculum matrix, module content owners, the 80% assessment pass mark, the 30-day completion window for new joiners and role movers, the annual refresh cycle, and the escalation path for non-completion

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and the Chief HR Officer; the curriculum content is re-approved annually by Regulatory Counsel and immediately on any amendment to 29 CFR 2560.503-1 or new EBSA guidance

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Annual cycle assigned within 30 days of the plan year start and closed within 90 days of assignment; new joiners and role movers must complete within 30 days of the job-code change; fiduciary training for Benefits Committee members is completed before their first meeting and refreshed annually

Deadline reminders configured.value: LMS reminders at assignment, day 15, day 25 and day 29 to the learner, with manager escalation at day 30 and functional-leader escalation at day 45; a weekly completion dashboard runs for the whole 90-day cycle

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Curriculum versions with content sign-off, assignment and completion records with timestamps and scores, assessment item banks and attestations retained six years from the Form 5500 filing date per ERISA §107, and for the duration of employment plus six years for individual records

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Non-completion past day 45 is logged with the learner, manager, days overdue and the disposition — completed, access to claim-decisioning queues suspended, or escalated to the functional leader and reflected in performance review

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Head of Compliance signs off any decision to let an overdue learner keep adjudicating ERISA claims and any curriculum change made in response to a compliance failure

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every employee holding an in-scope job code at any point in the plan year, including joiners, leavers and movers, together with their LMS assignment and completion records and the Benefits Committee roster

Pass/fail thresholds.value: 98% completion of the annual curriculum within the 90-day cycle, 100% for claim decision-makers and Benefits Committee members, an 80% assessment pass mark, and zero learners adjudicating ERISA claims while past day 45 without a signed exception

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual; the test runs once after the cycle closes with 100% coverage of in-scope job codes, plus a quarterly joiner/mover check on the 30-day window

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must sit outside Compliance and Learning & Development and must not have authored any module or administered the LMS cycle

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual ERISA training workpaper (population extract from HRIS, LMS completion export, reconciliation, exception schedule, curriculum sign-offs) in the compliance evidence repository under Plan Year

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Role-to-curriculum matrix, curriculum content with regulatory footnotes, and a completion report by job code with dates and scores — the evidence an EBSA investigator asks for when a claims-handling failure is alleged to be systemic

Regulator response path.value: Head of Compliance owns the training-evidence response to EBSA and to state market conduct examiners; Chief HR Officer supplies the population data and General Counsel clears any statement linking a training gap to a claims failure

checklist.step: Refresh the role-to-curriculum matrix from the HRIS job-code list
actions: Export the current job-code catalogue from Workday with headcount per code and the owning function.

Mark each code in scope where the work touches an ERISA plan — claims decisioning, disability case management, retirement recordkeeping, benefits administration, plan accounting, participant correspondence, contact centre, and IT configuring plan systems.
Assign each in-scope code a curriculum: Core ERISA Awareness, Claims Procedure Deep Dive, Fiduciary Duties for Committee Members, Plan Reporting, or Plan Data Security.
Have each functional leader confirm their codes and headcount in writing before the cycle opens.
checklist.done: every job code carries an in/out call and, where in scope, an assigned curriculum confirmed by its functional leader.

checklist.step: Refresh the Core ERISA Awareness module content
actions: Cover what makes an arrangement an ERISA plan, who is a fiduciary by function, the §404(a)(1) duties of loyalty, prudence, diversification and following plan documents, and the personal liability that attaches under §409.

Teach the prudence standard as a process standard: the decision file must show the question, the alternatives, the data and its date, the advisers and the decision-maker — the outcome alone is not a defence.
Add the participant-facing duties: SPD content and delivery, the §104(b)(4) document-request right and the 30-day response, and the prohibition on interference with protected rights under §510.
Footnote each screen with the statute or regulation it teaches so learners can find the source.
checklist.done: the awareness module covers plan status, functional fiduciaries, the §404(a)(1) duties as a process standard, and participant rights, with clause footnotes.

checklist.step: Refresh the Claims Procedure Deep Dive for decision-makers
actions: Teach the 29 CFR 2560.503-1(f) clocks by plan type and the extension rules, including that the extension notice must be written and issued before the original period expires.
Walk the (g) and (j) notice content element by element with a compliant and a non-compliant specimen side by side.

Teach the (l) consequence plainly: fail to follow the procedure and the claimant is deemed to have exhausted administrative remedies and can go straight to court, and the plan loses deferential review.
Include the disability-specific rules — independence and impartiality of decision-makers, the pre-decision notice of new evidence, and the SSA-determination discussion requirement.
checklist.done: the claims module teaches the clocks, the (g)/(j) elements against specimens, the (l) consequence and the disability-specific rules.

checklist.step: Build the Fiduciary Duties module for Benefits Committee members
actions: Cover committee charter and authority, the §405 co-fiduciary liability rules, the §406 prohibited transactions and the exemptions relied on, and 29 CFR 2550.404a-1 for investment decisions.
Teach the documentation standard the committee will be judged by, using the plan's own prudence-file standard and a redacted example of a decision file that met it.
Cover the monitoring duty over delegates and service providers, and the 408(b)(2) fee-disclosure condition the committee must confirm.
Cover the abandoned-plan rules in 29 CFR 2578.1 and when a qualified termination administrator becomes relevant.
checklist.done: the fiduciary module covers co-fiduciary liability, prohibited transactions, investment duties, delegate monitoring and abandoned plans with a worked decision file.

checklist.step: Build the Plan Data Security module from Compliance Assistance Release 2021-01
actions: Teach the twelve EBSA Cybersecurity Program Best Practices as the standard the company and its recordkeepers are measured against.
Teach the EBSA Tips for Hiring a Service Provider so anyone involved in vendor selection asks about control audits, insurance and breach obligations.

Teach the EBSA Online Security Tips staff must pass on to participants, and the account-takeover red flags in retirement distributions — changed address followed by a distribution request being the classic pattern.
Include the internal incident-reporting path and the timeframe for reporting a suspected participant-data compromise.
checklist.done: the security module teaches the twelve best practices, the hiring tips, participant online-security tips and the account-takeover red flags.

checklist.step: Have Regulatory Counsel approve every module before deployment
actions: Read each module against the cited regulation and confirm no screen states a deadline, an appeal right or a content requirement that is out of date.
Confirm the specimens used are current form editions so learners are not trained on retired templates.
Sign the content approval naming the module id, version and the regulatory text version relied on.
Withhold approval where a module teaches a plan-specific practice as if it were the regulatory minimum.
checklist.done: each module version carries a dated counsel content approval naming the module id and the regulatory text relied on.

checklist.step: Load the curricula and wire the auto-assignment rules
actions: Load each approved module version and build the curricula, retiring prior versions so no learner can complete last year's content.
Configure assignment rules driven by the HRIS job-code feed so a new joiner or a role mover is auto-assigned within 24 hours of the job-code change.
Set the due date at 30 days from assignment for joiners and movers and at 90 days from the annual cycle assignment for everyone else.
Run a dry-run against a sample of job codes and confirm the right curriculum lands on the right learner before the cycle opens.
checklist.done: curricula are loaded, prior versions retired, and job-code-driven auto-assignment is dry-run verified with correct due dates.

checklist.step: Build assessments that test application rather than recall
actions: Write scenario items: a disability claim received on the 1st with an extension taken on the 46th day; a denial letter with no §502(a) statement; a distribution request following a same-week address change.
Set the pass mark at 80% with a maximum of three attempts, and randomise items from a bank so attempts differ.
Require a wrong answer to route the learner back to the relevant screen before re-attempt.
Pilot the assessment with 10 experienced staff and re-write any item where the correct answer is ambiguous.
checklist.done: scenario-based assessments are live at an 80% pass mark with a randomised bank, remediation routing and a completed pilot.

checklist.step: Launch the annual cycle and communicate the consequence of non-completion
actions: Assign the annual curriculum within 30 days of the plan year start to every in-scope learner and notify their managers with the team roster.
State plainly in the launch communication that claim decision-makers past day 45 have their decisioning entitlement suspended until completion.
Brief functional leaders on their completion targets — 100% for claim decision-makers and committee members, 98% overall.
Publish the weekly completion dashboard from launch day.
checklist.done: the cycle is assigned within 30 days of plan year start with managers briefed, consequences stated and a weekly dashboard live.

checklist.step: Deliver live fiduciary training to the Benefits Committee before its first meeting
actions: Schedule the session before the committee's first meeting of the plan year and require attendance of every voting member and every alternate.
Cover the current year's specific risks — recent EBSA enforcement themes, the plan's own audit findings and any open fiduciary breach.
Take an attendance register signed by each attendee and minute the session as a committee agenda item.
Deliver a catch-up session within 30 days for any member who missed it and record it against their name.
checklist.done: every committee member has attended the live session or a catch-up within 30 days, with a signed register and minuted agenda item.

checklist.step: Work the completion dashboard weekly and escalate on schedule
actions: Publish completion by function, job code and manager each week with days remaining on the cycle.
Escalate learners past day 30 to their manager by name and past day 45 to the functional leader with a required response date.
Reconcile the learner list weekly to the HRIS so leavers drop off and new joiners appear rather than skewing the rate.
Report the closing rate against the 98% and 100% targets to the Head of Compliance at cycle end.
checklist.done: weekly dashboards run to cycle close with day-30 and day-45 escalations issued and the learner list HRIS-reconciled.

checklist.step: Suspend claim-decisioning entitlements for overdue decision-makers
actions: Receive the day-45 overdue list of claim decision-makers from Compliance each week.
Remove the claim-decisioning entitlement in the identity platform for each name and confirm the claims platform reflects the removal the same day.
Restore the entitlement only on an LMS completion record, never on a manager's assurance that the learner will finish.
Record every suspension and restoration with timestamps for the audit trail.
checklist.done: every day-45 overdue decision-maker has a timestamped entitlement suspension, restored only against an LMS completion record.

checklist.step: Re-train immediately when a compliance failure points to a knowledge gap
actions: Review the notice-timeliness exceptions, claims content exceptions and audit findings each quarter for recurring themes by team.
Where a theme is a knowledge gap, commission a targeted module or a live session for that team within 30 days rather than waiting for the annual cycle.
Assign it as a mandatory out-of-cycle curriculum with its own 30-day due date and track it to 100%.
Record the link between the finding and the training in the issue's remediation evidence.
checklist.done: each recurring finding theme has a targeted out-of-cycle module deployed within 30 days and tracked to 100% completion.

checklist.step: Capture the annual attestation alongside training completion
actions: Require every in-scope learner to attest at course completion that they will apply the claims procedure timeframes and notice content as taught and will report any breach they become aware of.
Require Benefits Committee members to attest additionally to their fiduciary status, the conflicts they have disclosed and their duty to monitor delegates.
Store the attestation with the completion record and its timestamp.
Report any refusal to attest to the Head of Compliance the same week.
checklist.done: every completion carries a timestamped attestation, with the extended fiduciary attestation from committee members.

checklist.step: Close the cycle and retain the training evidence
actions: Export the final completion report by job code with names, assignment dates, completion dates and assessment scores.
File it with the curriculum versions, counsel content approvals, assessment item bank, attendance registers and attestations under Plan Year.
Apply the six-years-from-Form-5500-filing retention label required by ERISA §107 and hold individual records for employment plus six years.
Confirm retrievability by learner name, job code, module version and completion date so a single employee's history can be produced for an examiner.
checklist.done: the closed cycle's evidence is filed, retention-labelled and retrievable per learner, job code and module version.

testing.step: Build the in-scope learner population from HRIS, not from the LMS
actions: Extract every employee and long-term contractor holding an in-scope job code at any point in the plan year, with start date, job-code change dates and leave dates.
Independently re-apply the in-scope test to the job-code catalogue rather than accepting the existing matrix, and list any code you would scope in that Compliance scoped out.
Add Benefits Committee members and alternates from the committee roster, who may not hold an in-scope job code.
Sign the population as complete with extraction date, filters and row counts.
testing.done: a signed learner population is built from HRIS with the in-scope test independently re-applied and committee members added.

testing.step: Reconcile the HRIS population to LMS assignments
actions: Match every population row to an LMS assignment on employee id and list learners with no assignment at all.
List LMS assignments with no matching in-scope population row and establish whether the feed is over- or under-assigning.
Test the joiner/mover feed by tracing 15 job-code changes to an assignment created within 24 hours.
Clear every difference before sampling — an unassigned learner is a control failure, not a data issue.
testing.done: every in-scope learner reconciles to an assignment, with feed latency tested on 15 job-code changes.

testing.step: Draw the sample and document the selection
actions: Take 100% of claim decision-makers, 100% of Benefits Committee members and 100% of learners recorded as overdue at cycle close.
Add 30 learners by seeded random draw across the remaining in-scope population, stratified by function.
Add 100% of joiners and movers in the final quarter to test the 30-day window under load.
Record the seed, population sizes and selection date so the sample is reproducible.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers all decision-makers, committee members, overdue learners and recent joiners/movers.

testing.step: Re-perform the completion and score check on the sample
actions: For each sampled learner open the LMS transcript and read the assignment date, completion timestamp, module version and assessment score.
Confirm the module version completed is the counsel-approved current version, not a retired one carried over from a prior year.
Confirm the score meets the 80% pass mark and that the attempt count is within the limit.
Treat a completion recorded by an administrator override without an assessment result as a fail.
testing.done: each sampled transcript shows the current module version, a passing score within attempt limits and no unsupported override.

testing.step: Test the curriculum content against the current regulation
actions: Open the deployed module versions and check each stated deadline, appeal window and notice element against the current text of 29 CFR 2560.503-1.
Confirm the specimens used are current form editions and that no retired template is shown as compliant.
Confirm the (l) deemed-exhaustion consequence and the disability-specific requirements are actually taught, not merely listed on a contents page.
Record any out-of-date content as an exception with the affected learner population — everyone who completed that version.
testing.done: deployed content is verified against the current regulation, with any stale content tied to its completed-learner population.

testing.step: Verify the entitlement suspension actually happened for overdue decision-makers
actions: Take the day-45 overdue list and check the identity platform for a timestamped entitlement removal for each name.
Query the claims platform for determinations decided by those names after day 45 and list every one — that is the real risk this control exists to stop.
Confirm each restoration is supported by an LMS completion record dated before the restoration timestamp.
Check for any signed Head of Compliance exception permitting continued decisioning and confirm it names the individual and the period.
testing.done: every day-45 name has a verified suspension or a signed exception, and post-day-45 determinations are quantified.

testing.step: Trace committee fiduciary training to registers, minutes and attestations
actions: Confirm the live session occurred before the committee's first meeting of the plan year by reading the meeting calendar and the session date.
Match every committee member and alternate on the roster to a signed attendance register entry or a dated catch-up record within 30 days.
Confirm the session is minuted as an agenda item and that the fiduciary attestation is on file for each member.
Flag any member who voted on a fiduciary decision before completing the training.
testing.done: every committee member traces to attendance or a 30-day catch-up, a minuted session and a filed fiduciary attestation.

testing.step: Recompute completion rates and the 30-day joiner/mover window
actions: Recompute the overall completion rate against the signed HRIS population — not the LMS assigned population — and compare to the 98% target.
Recompute the decision-maker and committee rates against the 100% target.
For each sampled joiner and mover, recompute days from job-code change to completion and compare to the 30-day window, recording days over.
Recompute the cycle timing: assignment within 30 days of plan year start and closure within 90 days of assignment.
testing.done: completion rates and every 30-day and cycle-timing computation are independently recomputed with overruns quantified.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception naming the learner or population, the job code, the gap and the operational exposure it created.
Assign a root cause (job code not scoped, HRIS feed lag, manager did not escalate, content not refreshed after a regulatory change, override used to close a transcript) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, where an untrained decision-maker adjudicated claims, refer those determinations to Compliance for a quality re-review.
Carry every open exception into the next cycle's launch as a mandatory pre-assignment check.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and a claims re-review referral where decisioning was affected.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compare the recomputed completion rates to the 98% and 100% thresholds and the assessment pass rate to the 80% mark.
State the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — with workpaper references and the count of determinations made by untrained decision-makers.
Have the reviewer, who sits outside Compliance and Learning & Development and authored no module, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Compliance Committee and the Chief HR Officer at the next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under Plan Year.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with recomputed rates, a stated conclusion and a committee reporting date is filed in the repository.
